Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 29, verse 1 (part 1 of 3):

His saying: ﴿Say: Tell me﴾ — that is, inform me — ﴿if Allah makes the night perpetual over you﴾. *Sarmad* (perpetual, continuous) means what is lasting and uninterrupted, from *al-sard* (succession), and the *mim* is augmentative. From it is the verse of Tarafah:

*"By your life, my affair is not a veil over you, neither my day nor my night is perpetual over you."*

It is said that its *mim* is original, and its form is *fa'lal* (فَعْلَلٌ), not *fa'mal* (فَعْمَلٌ), and this is the apparent view. He, glorified is He, showed them that He had prepared for them the means of livelihood so that they might give thanks for the blessing. For if the age in which they live were a night perpetual until the Day of Resurrection, they would not be able to move about in it and seek what they must have for sustenance, such as food, drink and clothing. Then He bestowed favour upon them and said: ﴿What god other than Allah will bring you light?﴾ That is: Is there any god among the deities you worship who is able to lift this perpetual darkness from you by means of *ḍiyā'* (light), meaning by a light in which you seek livelihood, see what you need, have your fruits made good, have your crops grow, and have your animals live? ﴿Will you not then listen?﴾ — listen to this speech with understanding, acceptance, reflection and contemplation.

Then, when He had finished bestowing favour upon them through the existence of the day, He bestowed favour upon them through the existence of the night, saying: ﴿Say: Tell me, if Allah makes the day perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection﴾ — that is, He makes the whole age in which you live a day until the Day of Resurrection — ﴿what god other than Allah will bring you a night in which you rest﴾ — that is, in which you settle, from fatigue and exhaustion, and rest from what you toil at in seeking livelihood and gain. ﴿Will you not then see?﴾ — see this great benefit with the sight of one who takes warning and is awake, so that you may desist from what you are in of worshipping other than Allah. When they acknowledge that none is able to do that except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, the proof is established against them and what they hold to of the falling doubts is nullified. Glorified is He, He joined *"will you not listen"* to the light, because hearing perceives what sight does not perceive, namely the grasp of its benefits and the description of its advantages; and He joined *"will you not see"* to the night, because sight perceives what hearing does not perceive of that.

﴿And of His mercy He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein﴾ — that is, in the night — ﴿and that you may seek of His bounty﴾ — that is, in the day, by striving in gains — ﴿and that perhaps you may give thanks﴾ — that is, so that you may give thanks for Allah's blessing upon you. This verse is of the type of *al-laff wa-al-nashr* (arrangement in which two items are mentioned and then each is assigned to its counterpart), as in the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

*"As if the hearts of the birds, moist and dry, beside their nest were ripe jujube and withered dry dates."*

Know that although rest in the day is possible, and seeking provision at night is possible — namely when the moon rises over the earth, or when one is lit by something that has light, like a lamp — yet that is rare and uncommon, contrary to what the servants are accustomed to, so no consideration is given to it.

﴿And on the Day when He calls to them, and says: Where are My partners whom you used to claim?﴾ Glorified is He, He repeated this because the two states differ: they are called once and they call upon the idols, and they are called another time and they fall silent. In this repetition there is also rebuke after rebuke and reproach after reproach.

His saying: ﴿And We will draw out from every nation a witness﴾ is coordinated with *yunādī* (He calls), and it came in the past tense to indicate certainty. The meaning is: We will bring out from every nation of the nations a witness who will testify against them.

Mujahid said: they are the prophets. It is also said: the just ones of every nation. The first is preferable.

Similar to it is His saying, glorified is He: ﴿How then, when We bring from every nation a witness, and bring you as a witness against these?﴾ [al-Nisa': 41]. Then He, glorified is He, explained what He will say to each nation of these nations by His saying: ﴿Then We will say: Bring your proof﴾ — that is, your argument and evidence that there are partners with Me. At that they confess and are struck dumb from producing proof. Therefore He said: ﴿Then they will know that the truth belongs to Allah﴾ in divinity, and that He alone has no partner, ﴿and what they used to fabricate has gone astray from them﴾ — that is, what they used to invent of falsehood in the world, that Allah has partners who deserve worship, has vanished from them, has been nullified and has gone away.

Then, glorified is He, followed the account of the people of misguidance with the story of Qarun, because of what it contains of wondrous power and marvellous making. So He said: ﴿Indeed, Qarun was of the people of Musa﴾. Qarun, on the pattern of *fa'ūl* (فاعُولٌ), is a non-Arabic proper noun, prohibited from declension by foreignness and being a proper name, and it is not an Arabic word derived from *qaranta* (I joined).

Al-Zajjaj said: If Qarun were from *qaranta al-shay'* (I joined the thing), it would be declinable.

Al-Nakha'i, Qatadah and others said: He was the paternal cousin of Musa. He was Qarun ibn Yasahar ibn Qahith ibn Lawi ibn Ya'qub, and Musa is the son of Imran ibn Qahith.

Ibn Ishaq said: He was the paternal uncle of Musa, full brother of his father and mother; he made him a brother of Imran, and both were sons of Qahith. It is also said: he was the maternal cousin of Musa. There was no one among the Children of Israel who knew the Torah better than him. So he became a hypocrite, as the Samiri became a hypocrite, and he went out from the obedience of Musa. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿So he oppressed them﴾ — that is, he exceeded the limit in arrogance and haughtiness toward them, rebelled against them, came out from the obedience of Musa, and disbelieved in Allah.

Al-Dahhak said: His oppression of the Children of Israel was his belittling them because of the abundance of his wealth and children.

Qatadah said: His oppression was his attributing what Allah had given him of wealth to himself, because of his knowledge and cunning.

It is also said: he was an agent of Pharaoh over the Children of Israel, and he transgressed against them and wronged them. It is also said that his oppression was other than that, which does not suit the meaning of the verse.

﴿And We gave him of the treasures﴾ — plural of *kanz*, which is wealth that has been stored up.

Ata' said: He came upon a treasure from the treasures of Yusuf. It is also said: he used to practise alchemy. And *mā* in His saying ﴿that the keys thereof﴾ is a relative pronoun, its relative clause being *inna* and what is within its scope, and for this reason *inna* is kasra-marked.

Al-Akhfash al-Saghir transmitted from the Kufans the prohibition of making a kasra-marked *inna* and what is within its scope a relative clause of *alladhi*, and he found this objectionable of them, since it occurs in the Mighty Book in this very place. *Mafatih* (keys) is the plural of *miftah* with a kasra, which is what is opened with; it is also said that what is meant by *mafatih* is the treasure-houses, in which case its singular is *mafṭah* with a fatha on the *mim*.

Al-Wahidi said: *Mafatih* means treasure-houses in the view of most exegetes, as in His saying: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the Unseen﴾ [al-An'am: 59]. He said: and this is the choice of al-Zajjaj, for he said: the more likely in interpretation is that *mafatihahu* are the treasure-houses of his wealth.

Others said: they are the plural of *miftah*, which is what the door is opened with. This is the view of Qatadah and Mujahid.

﴿Indeed, they would weigh down a band of men of great strength﴾. This clause is the predicate of *inna*, and *inna* with its subject and predicate is the relative clause of *mā*. It is said: *nā'a bi-ḥimlihi* means he rose up with it burdened; and *nā'a bī al-ḥimlu* means the load weighed me down. The meaning: the load of the keys burdens them.

Abu Ubaydah said: this is of the inverted construction (*al-maqlūb*), and the meaning is: the band would rise up with them, that is, they would stand up with them.

Abu Zayd said: *nu'tu bi-al-ḥimli* means when you rise up with the load. The poet said:

*"We have found a successor, a wretched successor, a slave who, when he rises with the load, halts."*

Al-Farra' said: the meaning of *tanū'u bi-al-'uṣbah* is that the load makes them lean with its weight, as is said: *yadhhabu bi-al-bu's* and *yadhhabu al-bu's* (he takes away the distress / the distress goes), *dhahabtu bihi* and *adhhabtuhu*, *ji'tu bihi* and *ajata'tuhu*, *nu'tu bihi* and *anata'tuhu*. Al-Nahhas chose this, and many of the early scholars said so.

It is also said that it is derived from *al-nay'*, which is distance, but this is far-fetched.

Budayl ibn Maysarah read *liyanū'a* with the *ya'* — that is, the one of them, or the one mentioned, would weigh down, and so it was taken according to the meaning. What is meant by *al-'uṣbah* is the group whose members support one another in partisanship.

It is said: it is from three to ten; it is said: from ten to fifteen; it is said: between ten and twenty; it is said: from five to ten; it is said: forty; it is said: seventy; and it is said: other than that.

﴿When his people said to him: Do not exult﴾. The adverbial phrase is in the accusative, governed by *tanū'u*. It is said it is governed by *ātaynāhu*, and it is said by *baghā*. Abu Hayyan rejected both, since giving and rebellion did not occur at that time.

Ibn Jarir said: it is connected with an omitted verb, which is *udhkur* (mention), and what is meant by "his people" here are the believers from the Children of Israel.

Al-Farra' said: it is Musa, and it is a plural used to mean the singular. The meaning of *lā tafraḥ* is: do not be insolent and do not be exultant. ﴿Indeed Allah does not love the exultant﴾ — the insolent and the exultant, who do not thank Allah for what He has given them.

Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is: do not exult in wealth, for one who exults in wealth does not pay its due. It is also said the meaning is: do not corrupt, as in the saying of the poet:

*"When you do not cease to discharge a trust, and carry another, the deposits have made you exult,"*

that is, they have corrupted you. Al-Zajjaj said: *al-fariḥīn* and *al-fāriḥīn* are the same. Al-Farra' said: *al-fariḥīn* are those who are in a state of exultation, and *al-fāriḥīn* are those who will exult in the future.

Mujahid said: the meaning of *lā tafraḥ* is: do not transgress. ﴿Indeed Allah does not love the exultant﴾ — the transgressors.

It is also said its meaning is: do not be stingy; indeed Allah does not love the stingy.

﴿And seek, in what Allah has given you, the Abode of the Hereafter﴾ — that is, seek in the wealth Allah has given you the Abode of the Hereafter, so spend it in what pleases Allah, not in arrogance and rebellion.

It was also read *wa-attabi'* (and follow).

﴿And do not forget your share of the world﴾. Most exegetes said: it is that you act in your world for your Hereafter, and a person's share is his lifespan and his righteous deeds.

Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is: do not forget to act for your Hereafter, because the reality of a person's share of the world is that by which he acts for his Hereafter.

Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: its meaning is: do not neglect your portion of your world in enjoying the lawful and seeking it. This is closer to the sense of the Qur'anic wording.

﴿And do good as Allah has done good to you﴾ — that is, do good to the servants of Allah as Allah has done good to you by the blessings of this world with which He has favoured you. It is also said: obey Allah and worship Him as He has favoured you. This is supported by what is established in the two Sahihs and others: that Jibril asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about *al-iḥsān* (excellence), and he said: "That you worship Allah as though you see Him; and if you do not see Him, then indeed He sees you."

﴿And do not seek corruption in the earth﴾ — that is, do not act in it with disobedience to Allah. ﴿Indeed Allah does not love the corrupters﴾ in the earth.

﴿He said: I have only been given it on knowledge that is with me﴾. Qarun said this in reply to the one who advised him with what came before: that is, I was only given what I was given of wealth on account of my knowledge. So his saying *'alā 'ilm* (on knowledge) is in the accusative place as a circumstantial phrase, and *'indī* (with me) is either an adverbial complement of *ūtītuhu* or a qualifier of *'ilm*. This is the knowledge which he made the cause of what he obtained of the world.

It is said: it is the knowledge of the Torah. It is said: his knowledge of the ways of gain and trade. It is said: knowledge of treasures and hidden hoards. It is said: knowledge of alchemy. It is said: the meaning is: Allah gave me these treasures on knowledge from Him of my deserving them, because of the excellence of His knowledge of me.

Al-Zajjaj chose this and rejected all else.

Then Allah refuted his saying, saying: ﴿Did he not know that Allah had destroyed before him generations greater than him in strength and more abundant in gathering?﴾ By *al-qurūn* (generations) are meant the past nations, and the meaning of *akthar jam'an* (more abundant in gathering) is: more abundant than him in gathering wealth. Had wealth or strength indicated excellence, Allah would not have destroyed them.

It is also said: *al-quwwah* means instruments, and *al-jam'* means helpers.

This statement is in the form of rebuke and reproach to Qarun, for he had read the Torah and knew the knowledge of the earlier generations and how Allah, glorified is He, had destroyed them. ﴿And the guilty will not be asked about their sins﴾ — that is, they will not be asked a question seeking to make them ask for pardon, as in His saying: ﴿nor will they be asked to make amends﴾ [al-Nahl: 84; al-Rum: 57], and ﴿so they will not be among those who are reproached﴾ [Fussilat: 24]. They will only be asked a question of rebuke and reproach, as in His saying: ﴿By your Lord, We will surely question them all﴾ [al-Hijr: 92].

Mujahid said: the angels will not ask the guilty tomorrow, for they will be recognised by their marks, for they will be gathered with black faces and blue eyes.

Qatadah said: the guilty will not be asked about their sins because their sins are manifest and numerous, but they will enter the Fire.

It is also said: the guilty of this nation will not be asked about the sins of the earlier nations.

**[Part 2 of 3]**

﴿So he went out to his people in his adornment.﴾ The *fa'* (ف) is conjunctive, coordinating with "qala" (he said), and what lies between them is a parenthetical clause (*i'tiraD*). The phrase ﴿in his adornment﴾ (*fi zinatihi*) is connected to "kharaja" (went out), or to an omitted verb, and it is a circumstantial clause (*hal*) referring to the subject of "kharaja."

The exegetes have mentioned various reports about this adornment with which he went out. What is meant is that he went out in an adornment that dazzled whoever saw it. For this reason, those who beheld him wished that they had the like of it, as Allah relates about them in His words: ﴿Those who desired the life of this world and its adornment said, "Would that we had the like of what Qarun was given. Indeed, he is possessed of a great portion."﴾ That is, a abundant share of worldly life.

The scholars differed about who these people were who uttered this statement. It was said: they were among the believers of that time. It was also said: they were a people of the disbelievers.

﴿But those who had been given knowledge said,﴾ and they were the rabbis (*ahbar*) of the Children of Israel. They said to those who had wished: ﴿Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better﴾ — that is, the reward of Allah in the Hereafter is better than what you wish for ﴿for those who believe and do righteousness.﴾ So do not desire the transient goods of this world which do not endure. ﴿But none is granted it except the patient﴾ — that is, this statement which the rabbis uttered. It was said: the pronoun refers to the righteous deeds. It was also said: it refers to Paradise. ﴿except the patient,﴾ those who are steadfast in obedience to Allah, and who restrain themselves from desires.

﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home.﴾ It is said: "khasafa al-makan yakhsifu khusufan," meaning he went down into the earth; and "khasafa bihi al-ardha khasfan," meaning it made him disappear into it. The meaning is that Allah, glorified is He, made him and his home vanish into the earth. ﴿So he had no company to help him against Allah﴾ — that is, he had no group who would ward off that from him, nor was he himself ﴿among those who could defend themselves﴾ — among those who could protect themselves from what had befallen him of the sinking.

﴿And by morning, those who had wished to be in his place said﴾ — that is, from a short time ago, ﴿"Ah! It is Allah who extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it. Had Allah not been gracious to us, He would have caused the earth to swallow us! Ah! The disbelievers will not be successful."﴾ That is, each one of them says this, regretting what had proceeded from him of wishful desire.

Al-Nahhas said: The best of what has been said about this is what al-Khalil, Sibawayh, Yunus and al-Kisa'i said: that the people became aware and said, "Wai" (ويْ). The one who regrets among the Arabs says "wai" in the course of his remorse.

Al-Jawhari said: *wai* is an expression of wonder. It is also said *waykа* (ويْكَ), and *wai* may be followed by *ka'anna*, both the light and the heavy forms: *wai-ka'anna Allah* (ويْكَأنَّ اللَّهَ).

Al-Khalil said: it is separated; you say "wai," then you begin, saying "ka'anna."

Al-Farra' said: it is a word of affirmation, like your saying: "Do you not see the handiwork of Allah and His kindness?" It was also said: it is a word of alerting, in the position of *ala* (ألا, "indeed/behold"). Qutrub said: it is originally *wailaka* (ويْلُكَ), and its *lam* was dropped. From this is the saying of 'Antarah:

> "Indeed, it has healed my soul and cured its sickness: the words of the horsemen, 'Wai-ka, 'Antar, advance!'"

Ibn al-A'rabi said: the meaning of "wai-ka'anna Allah" is: "I know that Allah..."

Al-Qutaybi said: its meaning in the dialect of Himyar is "mercy." It was also said: it means "Did you not see?" (*alam tara*).

It is reported from al-Kisa'i that he said: it is a word of lamentation.

﴿Had Allah not been gracious to us﴾ with His mercy and protected us from the likes of what Qarun was upon of insolence and transgression, and had He not taken us to account for what had occurred from us of that wishful desire, ﴿He would have caused the earth to swallow us﴾ just as He caused it to swallow him.

Hafs read *lakhasafa* (لَخَسَفَ) in the active voice, while the rest read it in the passive voice. ﴿Ah! The disbelievers will not be successful﴾ — that is, they will not attain any of their objectives.

﴿That is the Last Abode.﴾ That is, Paradise. The pointing to it is to express its magnification and to emphasize its status, as if He said: "That which you have heard the report of, and whose matter has reached you." ﴿We shall assign it to those who do not desire haughtiness upon the earth﴾ — that is, exaltation and arrogance over the believers ﴿or corruption.﴾ That is, acting in disobedience to Allah, glorified is He, therein. The mention of haughtiness and corruption as indefinite nouns within the scope of negation indicates that they include everything that is described as haughtiness and as corruption, without restriction to any particular kind. As for corruption, it is clear that none of it is permissible, whatever form it takes. As for haughtiness, what is forbidden is that which is in the manner of arrogance toward others and of domineering over people. It does not include seeking high rank in truth and leadership in religion, nor love of fine clothing, a fine mount, or a fine dwelling.

﴿Whoever comes with a good deed will have better than it﴾ — and that is that Allah rewards him tenfold, up to seven hundredfold. ﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed — those who did evil deeds will not be recompensed except [with the like of] what they used to do.﴾ That is, except the like of what they used to do; the genitive noun (*mudaf*) has been omitted and the noun in the genitive (*mudaf ilayhi*) has been put in its place. The explanation of the meaning of this verse has already been given in Surat al-Naml.

﴿Indeed, He who has imposed upon you the Qur'an﴾ — the exegetes said: that is, He sent down the Qur'an to you.

Al-Zajjaj said: He made obligatory upon you the acting according to what the Qur'an requires. The implied sense of the statement is: He imposed upon you the rulings of the Qur'an and its obligations. ﴿Will surely return you to a place of return.﴾ The majority of exegetes said: that is, to Makkah.

Mujahid, Ikrimah, al-Zuhri and al-Hasan said: the meaning is: "He will surely return you to the Day of Resurrection," and this is the view preferred by al-Zajjaj. It is said: "Between me and you is the *ma'ad*," meaning the Day of Resurrection, because people return (*ya'udun*) therein alive.

Abu Malik and Abu Salih said: "He will surely return you to a place of return," that is, to Paradise. Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said the same, and it was also reported from Mujahid.

It was said: "to a place of return" means to death.

﴿Say, "My Lord knows best who has come with guidance and who is in clear error."﴾ This is a reply to the disbelievers of Makkah when they said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "You are in error." The intended meaning of "who has come with guidance" is the Prophet (ﷺ), and "who is in clear error" refers to the polytheists. However, it is better to interpret the verse in its general sense, and that Allah, glorified is He, knows the state of each of these two groups and will recompense each with what it deserves of good or evil.

﴿And you did not expect that the Book would be bestowed upon you﴾ — that is, you did not hope that We would send you to the servants and send down the Qur'an to you.

It was said: "You did not expect that the Book would be bestowed upon you" by your being returned to your place of return. The exception in His words, ﴿except as a mercy from your Lord,﴾ is disjunctive (*munqati'*), meaning: "But its being cast upon you is a mercy from your Lord." It may also be connected (*muttasil*), taking it according to the sense, as if it were said: "The Book was not cast upon you except for the sake of the mercy from your Lord."

The first is preferable, and al-Kisa'i and al-Farra' affirmed it. ﴿So never be a supporter of the disbelievers﴾ — that is, a helper to them. There is an implicit allusion in this to others from the community. It was also said: the meaning is, "Do not be a supporter of them by flattering them."

﴿And let them not avert you from the verses of Allah after they have been revealed to you.﴾ That is: O Muhammad, let not the disbelievers, with their statements, their lies and their harm, avert you from reciting the verses of Allah and acting upon them, after Allah has sent them down to you and they have been made obligatory upon you.

The majority read with a *fatha* on the *ya'* and a *damma* on the *sad* from *sadda-hu, yasudduhu*. 'Asim read with a *damma* on the *ya'* and a *kasra* on the *sad*, from *asadda-hu*, with the same meaning as *sadda-hu*.

﴿And call to your Lord﴾ — that is, call the people to Allah and to His monotheism, and to acting upon His obligations and avoiding His disobedience. ﴿And never be among the polytheists.﴾ There is an implicit allusion to others in this, as has preceded, because he (ﷺ) would never be among the polytheists under any circumstances.

Likewise is His saying: ﴿And do not invoke with Allah another god﴾ — for it is an implicit allusion to others.

Then Allah, glorified is He, spoke of His own essence in the singular and described it with permanence and everlastingness, saying: ﴿There is no deity except Him. Everything will perish except His Face.﴾ That is, every thing among things, whatever it may be, will perish, except His Essence (*dhat*).

Al-Zajjaj said: "His Face" is in the accusative case as an exception. Were it outside the Qur'an, it would be in the nominative, in the sense of "everything other than His Face will perish," as the poet said:

> "And every brother, the one who parts from him is his brother, by the life of your father, except the two Farqads."

The meaning is: every brother other than the two Farqads is parted from by his brother. ﴿To Him is the judgement﴾ — that is, the binding decree; He judges by what He wills and rules by what He intends. ﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾ at the Resurrection, so that He may recompense the good-doer for his goodness and the wrongdoer for his wrongdoing. There is no deity besides Him, glorified and exalted is He.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿perpetual (sarmadan)﴾, that he said: "Continuously."

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from him regarding ﴿and what they used to fabricate will be lost to them﴾ on the Day of Resurrection, that he said: "They used to lie in the world."

Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh reported from him also, regarding ﴿Indeed, Qarun was of the people of Musa﴾, that he said: "He was his cousin, and he used to pursue knowledge until he had gathered a store of knowledge. He remained in that condition until he rebelled against Musa and envied him. Musa said to him, 'Allah has commanded me to take the zakat.' He refused, and said, 'Musa wants to devour your wealth. He has brought you the prayer and brought you other things, and you have endured them; will you endure his taking your wealth?' They said, 'We will not endure it. What do you advise?' He said, 'I advise that we send to a prostitute among the prostitutes of the Children of Israel, and we send her to him, and she will accuse him of having wanted her for herself.' They sent to her and said, 'We will give you your price on condition that you testify against Musa that he committed fornication with you.' She said, 'Yes.' Qarun came to Musa and said, 'Gather the Children of Israel and inform them of what your Lord has commanded you.' He said, 'Yes.' So he gathered them, and they said to him, 'What has your Lord commanded you?' He said, 'He commanded me that you worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, and that you maintain the ties of kinship, such and such.' And he said, 'He commanded me that if one who is married commits adultery, he is to be stoned.' They said, 'Even if you are that one?' He said, 'Yes.' They said, 'Then you have committed adultery.' He said, 'I?' They sent for the woman, and she came. They said, 'What do you testify concerning Musa?' Musa said to her, 'I adjure you by Allah to speak the truth.' She said, 'As for when you adjure me by Allah, they called me and set a reward for me on condition that I would accuse you with myself, and I bear witness that you are innocent and that you are the Messenger of Allah.' Musa fell down in prostration weeping. Allah revealed to him, 'What makes you weep? We have given you authority over the earth; command it and it will obey you.' He raised his head and said, 'Seize them!' So it seized them up to their ankles, and they began saying, 'O Musa! O Musa!' He said, 'Seize them!' So it seized them up to their knees, and they began saying, 'O Musa! O Musa!' He said, 'Seize them!' So it seized them up to their necks, and they began saying, 'O Musa! O Musa!' He said, 'Seize them!' So it seized them and covered them. Allah revealed, 'O Musa, My servants asked you and humbled themselves before you, and you did not answer them. By My might, had they called upon Me, I would have answered them.'"

Ibn 'Abbas said: "That is His saying: ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home﴾; he was swallowed down into the lowest earth."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Khaythamah, who said: "The keys to Qarun's treasures were of leather, each key the size of a finger, each key for a separate storehouse. When he rode out, the keys were carried on seventy mules, white-blazed and white-legged."

Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn al-Mundhir reported from him, who said: "I found in the Gospel that the mules bearing the keys to Qarun's storehouses were white-blazed and white-legged, and no key of them exceeded a finger in size; for each key there was a treasure."

I say: I have not found in the Gospel what Khaythamah mentioned.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words ﴿would weigh down (la-tanu'u) with the band﴾ that he said: "It burdens." 

Ibn al-Mundhir reported from him also: "The band of men of strength would not be able to lift them."

Ibn Jarir reported from him also: "The band is forty men."

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from him also, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the exultant (al-farihin)﴾: "The arrogant (al-marihin)." And regarding His words ﴿And do not forget your share of the world﴾: "That you work in it for your Hereafter."

Ibn Mardawayh reported from Aws ibn Aws al-Thaqafi, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding His words ﴿So he went out to his people in his adornment﴾: "In four thousand mules."

Reports have come from a group of the Successors (*tabi'un*) with statements explaining what he went out with, of adornment, to his people; but none of them is authentically traced to the Prophet (ﷺ). Rather, they are from the reports of the People of the Book, as we have explained to you on more than one occasion. I do not know how the chain (*isnad*) of this hadith is that Ibn Mardawayh traced to the Prophet (ﷺ). Whoever obtains his book, let him examine it.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 29, verse 1 (part 3 of 3):

It is related by al-Firyabi from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his house﴾, that he said: "He was swallowed down into the lowest earth."

It is related by al-Mahamili and al-Daylami in Musnad al-Firdaws from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), regarding His words ﴿That is the abode of the Hereafter. We assign it to those who do not seek exaltation in the earth or corruption﴾, that he said: "Arrogance in the earth and taking by other than the truth."

Something similar is narrated from Muslim al-Batin, Ibn Jurayj and ʿIkrimah.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿who do not seek exaltation in the earth﴾, that he said: "Tyranny in the earth."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Hasan, who said: "It is high rank and elevation in the eyes of their rulers."

I say: If that is for the purpose of strengthening oneself thereby upon the truth, then it is among the qualities of goodness, not among the qualities of evil.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, who said: "A man may love that the thong of his sandal be better than the thong of his companion's sandal, and so he would enter under this verse: ﴿That is the abode of the Hereafter. We assign it to those who do not seek exaltation in the earth or corruption﴾." Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir, after mentioning this report from ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him): "This is to be understood as applying to one who loves that for its own sake, not merely for adornment; that is not objectionable, for it is established that a man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I love that my garment be fine and my sandal be fine. Is that from pride?' He said: 'No, indeed Allah is beautiful and loves beauty.'"

Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn ʿAsakir related from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib that he said: "This verse, meaning ﴿That is the abode of the Hereafter﴾ etc., was revealed concerning the people of justice and humility among the rulers and those of power among all other people."

Ibn Mardawayh related something similar from Ibn ʿAbbas.

Ibn Mardawayh related from ʿAdi ibn Hatim, who said: "When he came in to the Prophet (ﷺ), he threw him a cushion, but he sat on the ground and said: 'I testify that you do not seek exaltation in the earth or corruption,' and he embraced Islam."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Dahhak.

Also Ibn Mardawayh related from ʿAli ibn al-Husayn ibn Waqid that His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, He who has ordained the Qur'an for you﴾ and the verse, "were revealed upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at al-Juhfah when the Prophet (ﷺ) set out as an emigrant to Madinah."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, al-Bukhari, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi related through several chains from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His words ﴿Will surely return you to a place of return﴾ that he said: "To Makkah." Ibn Mardawayh added: "As He brought you out of it."

Al-Firyabi, ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn Mardawayh related from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri regarding ﴿Will surely return you to a place of return﴾ that he said: "The Hereafter."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, al-Bukhari in his Tarikh, Abu Yaʿla and Ibn al-Mundhir related from him as well, regarding His words ﴿Will surely return you to a place of return﴾, that he said: "Its return is Paradise," and in another wording: "Its return is his Hereafter."

Al-Hakim in al-Tarikh and al-Daylami related from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, who said regarding ﴿Will surely return you to a place of return﴾: "Paradise."

Saʿid ibn Mansur, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh related something similar from Ibn ʿAbbas.

Ibn Mardawayh related from him that he said: When the verse ﴿Everyone upon it will perish﴾ [al-Rahman: 26] was revealed, the angels said: "The people of the earth have perished." When the verse ﴿Every soul shall taste death﴾ [Al ʿImran: 185] was revealed, the angels said: "Every soul has perished." When the verse ﴿Everything will perish except His Face﴾ was revealed (p-1113), the angels said: "The people of the heavens and the earth have perished."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd related from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding ﴿Everything will perish except His Face﴾ that he said: "Except what is intended by His Face."

The surah is disputed as Meccan or Medinan, or partly one and partly the other, on three opinions. The first is that it is entirely Meccan, related by Ibn al-Duraysi, al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il from Ibn Abbas. Ibn Mardawayh also related it from Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, and this is the view of al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Ata' and Jabir ibn Zayd. The second is that it is entirely Medinan. al-Qurtubi said this is one of two opinions of Ibn Abbas and of Qatadah. The third is that it is Meccan except for its first ten verses. al-Qurtubi said this is the other opinion of Ibn Abbas and Qatadah, and it is the view of Yahya ibn Sallam. It is also reported from Ali ibn Abi Talib that it was revealed between Mecca and Medina, which is a fourth opinion.

al-Daraqutni related in al-Sunan from Aisha that "the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would pray at the eclipse of the sun and the moon four bowings and four prostrations, reciting in the first rak'ah al-Ankabut or al-Rum, and in the second Ya-Sin."

﴿Alif Lam Mim.﴾ ﴿Do people think that they will be left to say, "We believe," and that they will not be tested?﴾ ﴿Indeed We tested those before them, and Allah will surely know those who are truthful, and He will surely know the liars.﴾ ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that they will outrun Us? Evil is what they judge.﴾ ﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah, indeed the term of Allah is coming, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ ﴿And whoever strives, he strives only for himself. Indeed Allah is Free of need from the worlds.﴾ ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will surely remove from them their misdeeds and We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do.﴾ ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents, but if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them. To Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do.﴾ ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds – We will surely admit them among the righteous.﴾ ﴿And among the people is he who says, "We believe in Allah," but when he is harmed for the sake of Allah, he regards the trial of people as like the punishment of Allah. But if victory comes from your Lord, they will surely say, "Indeed we were with you." Is not Allah most knowing of what is within the breasts of the worlds?﴾ ﴿And Allah will surely make evident those who believe, and He will surely make evident the hypocrites.﴾ ﴿And those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Follow our way, and we will bear your sins," but they will not bear anything of their sins. Indeed they are liars.﴾ ﴿And they will surely bear their burdens and burdens along with their burdens, and they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to fabricate.﴾

The discussion of the opening of this surah has already been given in full in Surat al-Baqarah. The interrogative in His words ﴿Do people think﴾ is for rebuke and reproach. ﴿That they will be left﴾ is in the accusative position governed by "hasiba" (thought). The phrase "hasiba" together with what follows it stands in place of the two objects, according to Sibawayh and the majority. ﴿That they will say, "We believe"﴾ is in the accusative position, with the sense of "li-an yaqulu" (so that they say), or "bi-an yaqulu" (by saying), or "ʿala an yaqulu" (on the condition that they say). It was also said that it is a substitute (badal) for "that they will be left." The meaning of the verse is that people are not left without being tested or tried, ﴿while they are not tested﴾, that is, they are not tried in their wealth and their selves. The matter is not as they thought. Rather, He must test them until the sincere is distinguished from the hypocrite and the truthful from the liar. The verse is therefore brought to deny that supposition and to show it to be far-fetched, and to make clear that testing by various kinds of obligations and other things is necessary.

al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is, "Did they think that We would be content with them saying only that they are believers and not be examined by that which makes the reality of their faith evident?" This is His words: ﴿that they will be left to say, "We believe," and that they will not be tested.﴾

al-Suddi, Qatadah and Mujahid said: that is, they will not be tried in their wealth and their selves through killing and torment. The explanation of the cause of revelation of these verses, which will come, clarifies the meaning of what we have mentioned. The apparent sense of the verses includes all people among the believers. Even if the cause is specific, the consideration is the generality of the wording, as we have established more than once.

Ibn Atiyyah said: although this verse was revealed concerning a specific cause, its ruling remains in the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) and is operative for the rest of time, because the trial from Allah continues on the frontiers of the Muslims through captivity, the attacks of the enemy, and other things.

﴿Indeed We tested those before them﴾: that is, this is the way of Allah with His servants, that He tests the believers of this community just as He tested those nations before them. This is what the Qur'an has brought in more than one place concerning the stories of the prophets, and what befell them and their peoples of trials, and what Allah tested their followers and those who believed in them with, of those matters that befell them. ﴿Allah will surely know those who are truthful﴾ in their saying, "We believe," ﴿and He will surely know the liars﴾ among them in that. The majority read "fa-la-yaʿlamanna" with a fatha on the ya and the lam in both places, meaning that Allah will make manifest the truthful and the liar in their saying and will distinguish between them. ʿAli ibn Abi Talib read it in both places with a damma on the ya and a kasra on the lam.

The meaning: that is, He will inform the two groups in the Hereafter of their stations, or He will inform the people of the truthfulness of the truthful and expose the liars for their lying, or He will assign to each group a sign by which it becomes known and distinguished from others.

﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that they will outrun Us?﴾ that is, they will escape and overcome Us before We call them to account for what they do. This clause takes the place of the two objects of "hasiba." "Am" here is the disjunctive (munqati'ah) "am." ﴿Evil is what they judge﴾, that is, wretched is what they judge, that judgment of theirs.

al-Zajjaj said: "ma" is in the accusative position with the sense of "saa" (evil) being a thing or a judgment that they judge. He said: it is also permissible that "ma" be in the nominative position with the sense of "evil is the thing or the judgment, their judgment." Ibn Kaysan made it a verbal noun (masdariyyah), meaning "evil is their judgment."

﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah﴾: that is, whoever hopes. "Raja'" (hope) here means "tama'" (longing). Said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr. It was also said that "raja'" here means fear. al-Qurtubi said: the people of tafsir agreed that the meaning is, "whoever fears death." From this is the verse of al-Hudhali:

"When the hornet stings him, he does not hope for its sting."

al-Zajjaj said: the meaning of "whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah" is: whoever hopes for the reward of the meeting with Allah, that is, the reward of arriving at Him. So "raja'" in this sense means hope. ﴿Then indeed the term of Allah is coming﴾, that is, the term set for the resurrection is coming without doubt. Muqatil said: it means the Day of Resurrection, and the meaning is: let him work for that day, as in His words: ﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous work﴾ [al-Kahf: 110]. The "man" in this verse may be conditional, with the answer being "indeed the term of Allah is coming." It may also be relative, and the "fa" has entered its response, likening it to the conditional.

In the verse there is promise, warning, intimidation and encouragement that is evident. He is the All-Hearing of the words of His servants, the All-Knowing of what they conceal and what they make public.

﴿Whoever strives, he strives only for himself﴾: that is, whoever strives against the disbelievers and strives against his own self through patience in acts of obedience, he strives only for himself, that is, the reward of that is for him and not for another, and nothing of its benefit returns to Allah, glory be to Him. ﴿Indeed Allah is Free of need from the worlds﴾, so He has no need of their obedience, just as their disobedience does not harm Him.

It was also said: the meaning is that whoever strives against his enemy for his own sake, not seeking thereby the face of Allah, then Allah has no need of his striving. The first is preferable.

﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds – We will surely remove from them their misdeeds﴾: that is, We will cover them over for them with forgiveness because of the righteous deeds they did. ﴿And We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do﴾: that is, with the best reward for their deeds. It was also said: with the reward for the best of their deeds. The intent of "best" is merely the description and not the comparative, lest their reward for goodness be left unmentioned. It was also said: He gives them more than what they did and better than it, as in His words: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed, for him is ten times its like﴾ [al-An'am: 160].

﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents﴾: the accusative of "husnan" is as a qualifier of an omitted verbal noun, that is, an enjoining that is good, for emphasis, or by omitting the genitive: that is, possessing goodness.

This is the position of the Basrans. The Kufans said: its estimate is "We enjoined upon man that he do good," so it is an object of an omitted verb. From this is the poet's saying:

"I wondered at Dahmaa when she complains about us,
And at Abu Dahmaa when he advises us to do good to her, as if they feared us."

That is, he advises us that we should do good to her. Similar is the saying of al-Hutay'ah:

"I have advised the free heart of Barrah: good to the dog and evil to the mother-in-law."

al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is, "We enjoined upon man": that he should do toward his parents what is good. It was also said: it is a qualifier of an omitted noun, that is, "We enjoined upon him a matter that is good." It was also said: it is in the accusative position as an object by implicit transitivity (tadmin), meaning "We obligated him to goodness." It was also said: it is in the accusative by removal of the preposition, meaning "We enjoined him with goodness." It was also said: it is a verbal noun of an omitted verb, meaning "he is good, goodness." The meaning of the verse is: the charge to man concerning his parents, to be dutiful to them and to be kind to them.

The majority read "husnan" with a damma on the ha and sukun on the mim. Abu al-Rajaa, Abu al-Aliyah and al-Dahhak read it with fatha on both. al-Jahdari read "ihsanan," and so also in the Mushaf of Ubayy.

﴿And if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them﴾: that is, they ask you and compel you to associate with Me a god of which you have no knowledge that it is a god. So do not obey them. Indeed "there is no obedience to a created being in disobedience to the Creator." He expressed the negation of knowledge in place of the negation of divinity, because what its soundness is not known for, it is not permissible to follow, so how about what is known to be false? And if obedience to the two parents is not permissible in this demand, even with their striving upon him, then its impermissibility with mere demand without striving from them is more fitting. Attached to the request for association from them is all the disobedience of Allah, glory be to Him. So there is no obedience to them in what is disobedience to Allah, as has been authentically reported from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). ﴿To Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do﴾: that is, I will inform you of your good deeds and your bad deeds, and then I will reward each of you according to what he deserves.

The relative pronoun in His words "those who believe and do righteous deeds" is in the nominative position as the subject, and its predicate is ﴿We will surely admit them among the righteous﴾: that is, into the company of those firmly established in righteousness. It is permissible that it be in the accusative position by way of preoccupation (ishtighal). It is permissible that the meaning be: "We will surely admit them into the place of entry of the righteous," which is Paradise, as it was said. The first is preferable.

﴿And among the people is he who says, "We believe in Allah," but when he is harmed for the sake of Allah﴾: that is, in the matter of Allah and for His sake, as the people of disbelief do with the people of faith, and as the people of sin do with the people of obedience, by inflicting harm upon them for the sake of faith in Allah and acting upon what He commanded. ﴿He regards the trial of people﴾, which is what they inflict upon him of harm, ﴿as like the punishment of Allah﴾: that is, he became distressed by their harm, did not endure it, and made it in severity and magnitude like the punishment of Allah, so he obeyed the people as he obeys Allah. It was also said: this is the hypocrite, who when he is harmed for the sake of Allah turns back from the religion and disbelieves.

al-Zajjaj said: it is fitting for the believer to endure harm for the sake of Allah. ﴿But if victory comes from your Lord﴾: that is, victory from Allah for the believers, conquest and triumph over the enemies, and spoils that they gain from them. ﴿They will surely say, "Indeed we were with you"﴾: that is, we are entering with you into your religion and helping you against your enemy. So Allah refutes them and says: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of what is within the breasts of the worlds?﴾: that is, He, glory be to Him, is most knowing of what is in their breasts, of good and evil from them, so how do they make this false claim?

These are a people from among those whose faith was weak. When harm from the disbelievers touched them, they went along with them. And when the strength of Islam appeared and Allah gave victory to the believers in some battle, they said, "Indeed we were with you." It was also said: what is meant by this and what precedes it is the hypocrites.

Mujahid said: it was revealed concerning people who believed in Allah with their tongues. So when a trial from Allah or a calamity befell them, they were seduced.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 29, verses 2–13 (part 2 of 2):

al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: It was revealed concerning some hypocrites in Mecca who would profess faith, but when they were harmed they reverted to polytheism. The apparent reading is that this arrangement, from His saying "And among the people is he who says" up to His saying "And those who disbelieved said," was revealed concerning the hypocrites, because this is what the context makes apparent.

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah will surely know those who have believed, and He will surely know the hypocrites﴾, it is there to confirm and reinforce what precedes it. That is: Allah will surely distinguish between the two groups, and the sincerity of the sincere and the hypocrisy of the hypocrites will become manifest. The sincere believer is one who is not shaken by the harm that befalls him, who is patient for the sake of Allah with the patience due to Him, and who does not make the trial by people equal to the punishment of Allah.

The hypocrite, however, inclines this way and that. If harm from the disbelievers befalls him, he goes along with them, follows them, and disbelieves in Allah, Mighty and Majestic. But if the breeze of Islam blows (in his favor), his victory appears and his conquest shines forth, he returns to Islam and claims that he is among the Muslims.

(p-1115) ﴿And those who disbelieved said to those who believed, "Follow our way, and we will bear your sins."﴾ The lām in ﴿lilladhīna āmanū﴾ (to those who believed) is the lām of conveyance (lām al-tablīgh), meaning that they spoke to them directly, as has been explained in more than one place. That is: they said to them, "Take our path and enter into our religion." ﴿And we will bear your sins﴾: that is, if following our way is a sin for which you will be held to account at the resurrection and the gathering, as you claim, then let us bear that on your behalf and be held to account for it instead of you. The lām in ﴿wa-l-naḥmil﴾ (and let us bear) is the lām of command, as though they were commanding themselves to do so.

al-Farrā' and al-Zajjāj said: It is an imperative in the sense of a conditional and its consequence. That is: "If you follow our way, we will bear your sins." Then Allah answered them with His saying: ﴿But they will not bear anything of their sins﴾. The first ﴿min﴾ (of ﴿min khaṭāyāhum﴾) is explanatory (bayāniyya), and the second is extra (zā'ida) for generality (li-l-istighrāq): that is, they will not bear any part whatsoever of their sins, which they had obligated themselves to and guaranteed to bear for them. Then Allah, Glorified is He, described them with lying in this undertaking to bear the burden, saying: ﴿Indeed, they are liars in what they guaranteed of bearing your sins﴾.

al-Mahdawī said: This denial from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, was construed according to the meaning, because the meaning is: "If you follow our way, we will bear your sins." Since the command, in meaning, reverts to a statement of fact, the denial was applied to it, just as denial is applied to a statement of fact.

﴿And they will surely bear their own burdens﴾: that is, their wrongs which they committed. The expression of them as "burdens" indicates that they are great sins. ﴿And burdens along with their burdens﴾: that is, wrongs along with their wrongs. These are the wrongs of those whom they misled and drew away from guidance into error. Similar to this is His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿That they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and also some of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge﴾ [al-Naḥl: 25]. Similar to this is the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Whoever establishes an evil practice in Islam, upon him is its burden and the burden of whoever acts upon it," as in the hadith of Abū Hurayrah which is authentic in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim and elsewhere.

﴿And they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection﴾ as a rebuke and reproach, ﴿concerning what they used to fabricate﴾: that is, what they invented of lies which they used to bring forth in the world.

Muqātil said: It refers to their saying, "We are the guarantors for every consequence that befalls you from Allah."

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted, concerning His saying: ﴿Alif-Lām-Mīm. Do the people think that they will be left⦆ to the end of the verse, that he said: It was revealed concerning some people in Mecca who had professed Islam. The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Medina wrote to them when the verse of emigration was revealed, that no profession or Islam would be accepted from them until they emigrated. He said: So they set out intending to go to Medina, but the polytheists pursued them and turned them back. Then this verse was revealed concerning them. They wrote to them that such-and-such had been revealed concerning them. They said: "We will go out, and if anyone follows us, we will kill him." So they went out, the polytheists pursued them, and they fought them. Some of them were killed and some escaped. Then Allah revealed concerning them: ﴿Then indeed your Lord — for those who emigrated after they had been tried, then struggled and were patient — indeed your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Naḥl: 110].

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted similarly from Qatādah, more briefly. Ibn Saʿd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Ibn ʿAsākir transmitted from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmayr who said: It was revealed concerning ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir when he was being tortured for the sake of Allah: ﴿Alif-Lām-Mīm. Do the people think that they will be left⦆ to the end of the verse.

Ibn Mājah and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn Masʿūd who said: The first whose Islam Allah made manifest were seven: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Abū Bakr, Sumayyah the mother of ʿAmmār, ʿAmmār, Ṣuhayb, Bilāl and al-Miqdād.

As for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Allah protected him through his uncle Abū Ṭālib; as for Abū Bakr, Allah protected him through his people; as for the rest, the polytheists seized them, put coats of iron mail on them and exposed them to the sun. There was not one of them but that he had complied with what they wanted, except Bilāl, for his soul was made light to him for the sake of Allah, and he was held lightly by his people. So they seized him and gave him to the boys, and they began to drag him around the valleys of Mecca while he kept saying: "One! One!"

al-Firyābī, Ibn Abī Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Mujāhid concerning His saying ﴿that they could outrun us﴾ that he said: that they could overpower us.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ who said: My mother said, "I will not eat any food or drink any drink until you disbelieve in Muḥammad." She refrained from food and drink until they began to force her mouth open with a stick. Then this verse was revealed: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents; but if they strive to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them﴾.

al-Tirmidhī also transmitted this from him, and said: "Four verses were revealed concerning me," and he mentioned something similar to this story, and said: "Ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ."

Aḥmad, Muslim, Abū Dāwūd and al-Nasā'ī also transmitted this hadith.

Aḥmad, Ibn Abī Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, al-Tirmidhī (who graded it ṣaḥīḥ), Ibn Mājah, Abū Yaʿlā, Ibn Ḥibbān, Abū Nuʿaym, al-Bayhaqī and al-Ḍiyāʾ transmitted from Anas who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I was harmed for the sake of Allah, and no one is harmed as I am; I was frightened for the sake of Allah, and no one is frightened as I am. Three nights passed over me when I and Bilāl had no food that any living thing could eat, except what was concealed under Bilāl's armpit."

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His saying: ﴿He makes the trial of people equal to the punishment of Allah﴾ that he said: He apostatizes from the religion of Allah when he is harmed for the sake of Allah.

The surah is disputed as Meccan or Medinan, or partly one and partly the other, on three opinions. The first is that it is entirely Meccan, related by Ibn al-Duraysi, al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il from Ibn Abbas. Ibn Mardawayh also related it from Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, and this is the view of al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Ata' and Jabir ibn Zayd. The second is that it is entirely Medinan. al-Qurtubi said this is one of two opinions of Ibn Abbas and of Qatadah. The third is that it is Meccan except for its first ten verses. al-Qurtubi said this is the other opinion of Ibn Abbas and Qatadah, and it is the view of Yahya ibn Sallam. It is also reported from Ali ibn Abi Talib that it was revealed between Mecca and Medina, which is a fourth opinion.

al-Daraqutni related in al-Sunan from Aisha that "the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would pray at the eclipse of the sun and the moon four bowings and four prostrations, reciting in the first rak'ah al-Ankabut or al-Rum, and in the second Ya-Sin."

﴿Alif Lam Mim.﴾ ﴿Do people think that they will be left to say, "We believe," and that they will not be tested?﴾ ﴿Indeed We tested those before them, and Allah will surely know those who are truthful, and He will surely know the liars.﴾ ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that they will outrun Us? Evil is what they judge.﴾ ﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah, indeed the term of Allah is coming, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ ﴿And whoever strives, he strives only for himself. Indeed Allah is Free of need from the worlds.﴾ ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will surely remove from them their misdeeds and We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do.﴾ ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents, but if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them. To Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do.﴾ ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds – We will surely admit them among the righteous.﴾ ﴿And among the people is he who says, "We believe in Allah," but when he is harmed for the sake of Allah, he regards the trial of people as like the punishment of Allah. But if victory comes from your Lord, they will surely say, "Indeed we were with you." Is not Allah most knowing of what is within the breasts of the worlds?﴾ ﴿And Allah will surely make evident those who believe, and He will surely make evident the hypocrites.﴾ ﴿And those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Follow our way, and we will bear your sins," but they will not bear anything of their sins. Indeed they are liars.﴾ ﴿And they will surely bear their burdens and burdens along with their burdens, and they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to fabricate.﴾

The discussion of the opening of this surah has already been given in full in Surat al-Baqarah. The interrogative in His words ﴿Do people think﴾ is for rebuke and reproach. ﴿That they will be left﴾ is in the accusative position governed by "hasiba" (thought). The phrase "hasiba" together with what follows it stands in place of the two objects, according to Sibawayh and the majority. ﴿That they will say, "We believe"﴾ is in the accusative position, with the sense of "li-an yaqulu" (so that they say), or "bi-an yaqulu" (by saying), or "ʿala an yaqulu" (on the condition that they say). It was also said that it is a substitute (badal) for "that they will be left." The meaning of the verse is that people are not left without being tested or tried, ﴿while they are not tested﴾, that is, they are not tried in their wealth and their selves. The matter is not as they thought. Rather, He must test them until the sincere is distinguished from the hypocrite and the truthful from the liar. The verse is therefore brought to deny that supposition and to show it to be far-fetched, and to make clear that testing by various kinds of obligations and other things is necessary.

al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is, "Did they think that We would be content with them saying only that they are believers and not be examined by that which makes the reality of their faith evident?" This is His words: ﴿that they will be left to say, "We believe," and that they will not be tested.﴾

al-Suddi, Qatadah and Mujahid said: that is, they will not be tried in their wealth and their selves through killing and torment. The explanation of the cause of revelation of these verses, which will come, clarifies the meaning of what we have mentioned. The apparent sense of the verses includes all people among the believers. Even if the cause is specific, the consideration is the generality of the wording, as we have established more than once.

Ibn Atiyyah said: although this verse was revealed concerning a specific cause, its ruling remains in the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) and is operative for the rest of time, because the trial from Allah continues on the frontiers of the Muslims through captivity, the attacks of the enemy, and other things.

﴿Indeed We tested those before them﴾: that is, this is the way of Allah with His servants, that He tests the believers of this community just as He tested those nations before them. This is what the Qur'an has brought in more than one place concerning the stories of the prophets, and what befell them and their peoples of trials, and what Allah tested their followers and those who believed in them with, of those matters that befell them. ﴿Allah will surely know those who are truthful﴾ in their saying, "We believe," ﴿and He will surely know the liars﴾ among them in that. The majority read "fa-la-yaʿlamanna" with a fatha on the ya and the lam in both places, meaning that Allah will make manifest the truthful and the liar in their saying and will distinguish between them. ʿAli ibn Abi Talib read it in both places with a damma on the ya and a kasra on the lam.

The meaning: that is, He will inform the two groups in the Hereafter of their stations, or He will inform the people of the truthfulness of the truthful and expose the liars for their lying, or He will assign to each group a sign by which it becomes known and distinguished from others.

﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that they will outrun Us?﴾ that is, they will escape and overcome Us before We call them to account for what they do. This clause takes the place of the two objects of "hasiba." "Am" here is the disjunctive (munqati'ah) "am." ﴿Evil is what they judge﴾, that is, wretched is what they judge, that judgment of theirs.

al-Zajjaj said: "ma" is in the accusative position with the sense of "saa" (evil) being a thing or a judgment that they judge. He said: it is also permissible that "ma" be in the nominative position with the sense of "evil is the thing or the judgment, their judgment." Ibn Kaysan made it a verbal noun (masdariyyah), meaning "evil is their judgment."

﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah﴾: that is, whoever hopes. "Raja'" (hope) here means "tama'" (longing). Said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr. It was also said that "raja'" here means fear. al-Qurtubi said: the people of tafsir agreed that the meaning is, "whoever fears death." From this is the verse of al-Hudhali:

"When the hornet stings him, he does not hope for its sting."

al-Zajjaj said: the meaning of "whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah" is: whoever hopes for the reward of the meeting with Allah, that is, the reward of arriving at Him. So "raja'" in this sense means hope. ﴿Then indeed the term of Allah is coming﴾, that is, the term set for the resurrection is coming without doubt. Muqatil said: it means the Day of Resurrection, and the meaning is: let him work for that day, as in His words: ﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous work﴾ [al-Kahf: 110]. The "man" in this verse may be conditional, with the answer being "indeed the term of Allah is coming." It may also be relative, and the "fa" has entered its response, likening it to the conditional.

In the verse there is promise, warning, intimidation and encouragement that is evident. He is the All-Hearing of the words of His servants, the All-Knowing of what they conceal and what they make public.

﴿Whoever strives, he strives only for himself﴾: that is, whoever strives against the disbelievers and strives against his own self through patience in acts of obedience, he strives only for himself, that is, the reward of that is for him and not for another, and nothing of its benefit returns to Allah, glory be to Him. ﴿Indeed Allah is Free of need from the worlds﴾, so He has no need of their obedience, just as their disobedience does not harm Him.

It was also said: the meaning is that whoever strives against his enemy for his own sake, not seeking thereby the face of Allah, then Allah has no need of his striving. The first is preferable.

﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds – We will surely remove from them their misdeeds﴾: that is, We will cover them over for them with forgiveness because of the righteous deeds they did. ﴿And We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do﴾: that is, with the best reward for their deeds. It was also said: with the reward for the best of their deeds. The intent of "best" is merely the description and not the comparative, lest their reward for goodness be left unmentioned. It was also said: He gives them more than what they did and better than it, as in His words: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed, for him is ten times its like﴾ [al-An'am: 160].

﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents﴾: the accusative of "husnan" is as a qualifier of an omitted verbal noun, that is, an enjoining that is good, for emphasis, or by omitting the genitive: that is, possessing goodness.

This is the position of the Basrans. The Kufans said: its estimate is "We enjoined upon man that he do good," so it is an object of an omitted verb. From this is the poet's saying:

"I wondered at Dahmaa when she complains about us,
And at Abu Dahmaa when he advises us to do good to her, as if they feared us."

That is, he advises us that we should do good to her. Similar is the saying of al-Hutay'ah:

"I have advised the free heart of Barrah: good to the dog and evil to the mother-in-law."

al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is, "We enjoined upon man": that he should do toward his parents what is good. It was also said: it is a qualifier of an omitted noun, that is, "We enjoined upon him a matter that is good." It was also said: it is in the accusative position as an object by implicit transitivity (tadmin), meaning "We obligated him to goodness." It was also said: it is in the accusative by removal of the preposition, meaning "We enjoined him with goodness." It was also said: it is a verbal noun of an omitted verb, meaning "he is good, goodness." The meaning of the verse is: the charge to man concerning his parents, to be dutiful to them and to be kind to them.

The majority read "husnan" with a damma on the ha and sukun on the mim. Abu al-Rajaa, Abu al-Aliyah and al-Dahhak read it with fatha on both. al-Jahdari read "ihsanan," and so also in the Mushaf of Ubayy.

﴿And if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them﴾: that is, they ask you and compel you to associate with Me a god of which you have no knowledge that it is a god. So do not obey them. Indeed "there is no obedience to a created being in disobedience to the Creator." He expressed the negation of knowledge in place of the negation of divinity, because what its soundness is not known for, it is not permissible to follow, so how about what is known to be false? And if obedience to the two parents is not permissible in this demand, even with their striving upon him, then its impermissibility with mere demand without striving from them is more fitting. Attached to the request for association from them is all the disobedience of Allah, glory be to Him. So there is no obedience to them in what is disobedience to Allah, as has been authentically reported from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). ﴿To Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do﴾: that is, I will inform you of your good deeds and your bad deeds, and then I will reward each of you according to what he deserves.

The relative pronoun in His words "those who believe and do righteous deeds" is in the nominative position as the subject, and its predicate is ﴿We will surely admit them among the righteous﴾: that is, into the company of those firmly established in righteousness. It is permissible that it be in the accusative position by way of preoccupation (ishtighal). It is permissible that the meaning be: "We will surely admit them into the place of entry of the righteous," which is Paradise, as it was said. The first is preferable.

﴿And among the people is he who says, "We believe in Allah," but when he is harmed for the sake of Allah﴾: that is, in the matter of Allah and for His sake, as the people of disbelief do with the people of faith, and as the people of sin do with the people of obedience, by inflicting harm upon them for the sake of faith in Allah and acting upon what He commanded. ﴿He regards the trial of people﴾, which is what they inflict upon him of harm, ﴿as like the punishment of Allah﴾: that is, he became distressed by their harm, did not endure it, and made it in severity and magnitude like the punishment of Allah, so he obeyed the people as he obeys Allah. It was also said: this is the hypocrite, who when he is harmed for the sake of Allah turns back from the religion and disbelieves.

al-Zajjaj said: it is fitting for the believer to endure harm for the sake of Allah. ﴿But if victory comes from your Lord﴾: that is, victory from Allah for the believers, conquest and triumph over the enemies, and spoils that they gain from them. ﴿They will surely say, "Indeed we were with you"﴾: that is, we are entering with you into your religion and helping you against your enemy. So Allah refutes them and says: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of what is within the breasts of the worlds?﴾: that is, He, glory be to Him, is most knowing of what is in their breasts, of good and evil from them, so how do they make this false claim?

These are a people from among those whose faith was weak. When harm from the disbelievers touched them, they went along with them. And when the strength of Islam appeared and Allah gave victory to the believers in some battle, they said, "Indeed we were with you." It was also said: what is meant by this and what precedes it is the hypocrites.

Mujahid said: it was revealed concerning people who believed in Allah with their tongues. So when a trial from Allah or a calamity befell them, they were seduced.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 29, verses 2–13 (part 2 of 2):

al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: It was revealed concerning some hypocrites in Mecca who would profess faith, but when they were harmed they reverted to polytheism. The apparent reading is that this arrangement, from His saying "And among the people is he who says" up to His saying "And those who disbelieved said," was revealed concerning the hypocrites, because this is what the context makes apparent.

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah will surely know those who have believed, and He will surely know the hypocrites﴾, it is there to confirm and reinforce what precedes it. That is: Allah will surely distinguish between the two groups, and the sincerity of the sincere and the hypocrisy of the hypocrites will become manifest. The sincere believer is one who is not shaken by the harm that befalls him, who is patient for the sake of Allah with the patience due to Him, and who does not make the trial by people equal to the punishment of Allah.

The hypocrite, however, inclines this way and that. If harm from the disbelievers befalls him, he goes along with them, follows them, and disbelieves in Allah, Mighty and Majestic. But if the breeze of Islam blows (in his favor), his victory appears and his conquest shines forth, he returns to Islam and claims that he is among the Muslims.

(p-1115) ﴿And those who disbelieved said to those who believed, "Follow our way, and we will bear your sins."﴾ The lām in ﴿lilladhīna āmanū﴾ (to those who believed) is the lām of conveyance (lām al-tablīgh), meaning that they spoke to them directly, as has been explained in more than one place. That is: they said to them, "Take our path and enter into our religion." ﴿And we will bear your sins﴾: that is, if following our way is a sin for which you will be held to account at the resurrection and the gathering, as you claim, then let us bear that on your behalf and be held to account for it instead of you. The lām in ﴿wa-l-naḥmil﴾ (and let us bear) is the lām of command, as though they were commanding themselves to do so.

al-Farrā' and al-Zajjāj said: It is an imperative in the sense of a conditional and its consequence. That is: "If you follow our way, we will bear your sins." Then Allah answered them with His saying: ﴿But they will not bear anything of their sins﴾. The first ﴿min﴾ (of ﴿min khaṭāyāhum﴾) is explanatory (bayāniyya), and the second is extra (zā'ida) for generality (li-l-istighrāq): that is, they will not bear any part whatsoever of their sins, which they had obligated themselves to and guaranteed to bear for them. Then Allah, Glorified is He, described them with lying in this undertaking to bear the burden, saying: ﴿Indeed, they are liars in what they guaranteed of bearing your sins﴾.

al-Mahdawī said: This denial from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, was construed according to the meaning, because the meaning is: "If you follow our way, we will bear your sins." Since the command, in meaning, reverts to a statement of fact, the denial was applied to it, just as denial is applied to a statement of fact.

﴿And they will surely bear their own burdens﴾: that is, their wrongs which they committed. The expression of them as "burdens" indicates that they are great sins. ﴿And burdens along with their burdens﴾: that is, wrongs along with their wrongs. These are the wrongs of those whom they misled and drew away from guidance into error. Similar to this is His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿That they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and also some of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge﴾ [al-Naḥl: 25]. Similar to this is the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Whoever establishes an evil practice in Islam, upon him is its burden and the burden of whoever acts upon it," as in the hadith of Abū Hurayrah which is authentic in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim and elsewhere.

﴿And they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection﴾ as a rebuke and reproach, ﴿concerning what they used to fabricate﴾: that is, what they invented of lies which they used to bring forth in the world.

Muqātil said: It refers to their saying, "We are the guarantors for every consequence that befalls you from Allah."

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted, concerning His saying: ﴿Alif-Lām-Mīm. Do the people think that they will be left⦆ to the end of the verse, that he said: It was revealed concerning some people in Mecca who had professed Islam. The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Medina wrote to them when the verse of emigration was revealed, that no profession or Islam would be accepted from them until they emigrated. He said: So they set out intending to go to Medina, but the polytheists pursued them and turned them back. Then this verse was revealed concerning them. They wrote to them that such-and-such had been revealed concerning them. They said: "We will go out, and if anyone follows us, we will kill him." So they went out, the polytheists pursued them, and they fought them. Some of them were killed and some escaped. Then Allah revealed concerning them: ﴿Then indeed your Lord — for those who emigrated after they had been tried, then struggled and were patient — indeed your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Naḥl: 110].

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted similarly from Qatādah, more briefly. Ibn Saʿd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Ibn ʿAsākir transmitted from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmayr who said: It was revealed concerning ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir when he was being tortured for the sake of Allah: ﴿Alif-Lām-Mīm. Do the people think that they will be left⦆ to the end of the verse.

Ibn Mājah and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn Masʿūd who said: The first whose Islam Allah made manifest were seven: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Abū Bakr, Sumayyah the mother of ʿAmmār, ʿAmmār, Ṣuhayb, Bilāl and al-Miqdād.

As for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Allah protected him through his uncle Abū Ṭālib; as for Abū Bakr, Allah protected him through his people; as for the rest, the polytheists seized them, put coats of iron mail on them and exposed them to the sun. There was not one of them but that he had complied with what they wanted, except Bilāl, for his soul was made light to him for the sake of Allah, and he was held lightly by his people. So they seized him and gave him to the boys, and they began to drag him around the valleys of Mecca while he kept saying: "One! One!"

al-Firyābī, Ibn Abī Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Mujāhid concerning His saying ﴿that they could outrun us﴾ that he said: that they could overpower us.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ who said: My mother said, "I will not eat any food or drink any drink until you disbelieve in Muḥammad." She refrained from food and drink until they began to force her mouth open with a stick. Then this verse was revealed: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents; but if they strive to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them﴾.

al-Tirmidhī also transmitted this from him, and said: "Four verses were revealed concerning me," and he mentioned something similar to this story, and said: "Ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ."
