Aḥmad, Muslim, Abū Dāwūd and al-Nasā'ī also transmitted this hadith.

Aḥmad, Ibn Abī Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, al-Tirmidhī (who graded it ṣaḥīḥ), Ibn Mājah, Abū Yaʿlā, Ibn Ḥibbān, Abū Nuʿaym, al-Bayhaqī and al-Ḍiyāʾ transmitted from Anas who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I was harmed for the sake of Allah, and no one is harmed as I am; I was frightened for the sake of Allah, and no one is frightened as I am. Three nights passed over me when I and Bilāl had no food that any living thing could eat, except what was concealed under Bilāl's armpit."

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His saying: ﴿He makes the trial of people equal to the punishment of Allah﴾ that he said: He apostatizes from the religion of Allah when he is harmed for the sake of Allah.

Ibn Mardawayh also related it from Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, and this is the view of al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Ata' and Jabir ibn Zayd. The second is that it is entirely Medinan. al-Qurtubi said this is one of two opinions of Ibn Abbas and of Qatadah. The third is that it is Meccan except for its first ten verses. al-Qurtubi said this is the other opinion of Ibn Abbas and Qatadah, and it is the view of Yahya ibn Sallam. It is also reported from Ali ibn Abi Talib that it was revealed between Mecca and Medina, which is a fourth opinion.

Evil is what they judge.﴾ ﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah, indeed the term of Allah is coming, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ ﴿And whoever strives, he strives only for himself. The explanation of the cause of revelation of these verses, which will come, clarifies the meaning of what we have mentioned. The apparent sense of the verses includes all people among the believers. Even if the cause is specific, the consideration is the generality of the wording, as we have established more than once.

Ibn Atiyyah said: although this verse was revealed concerning a specific cause, its ruling remains in the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) and is operative for the rest of time, because the trial from Allah continues on the frontiers of the Muslims through captivity, the attacks of the enemy, and other things.

﴿Indeed We tested those before them﴾: that is, this is the way of Allah with His servants, that He tests the believers of this community just as He tested those nations before them. This is what the Qur'an has brought in more than one place concerning the stories of the prophets, and what befell them and their peoples of trials, and what Allah tested their followers and those who believed in them with, of those matters that befell them. ﴿Allah will surely know those who are truthful﴾ in their saying, "We believe," ﴿and He will surely know the liars﴾ among them in that. The majority read "fa-la-yaʿlamanna" with a fatha on the ya and the lam in both places, meaning that Allah will make manifest the truthful and the liar in their saying and will distinguish between them. ʿAli ibn Abi Talib read it in both places with a damma on the ya and a kasra on the lam.

The meaning: that is, He will inform the two groups in the Hereafter of their stations, or He will inform the people of the truthfulness of the truthful and expose the liars for their lying, or He will assign to each group a sign by which it becomes known and distinguished from others.

﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that they will outrun Us?﴾ that is, they will escape and overcome Us before We call them to account for what they do. This clause takes the place of the two objects of "hasiba." "Am" here is the disjunctive (munqati'ah) "am." ﴿Evil is what they judge﴾, that is, wretched is what they judge, that judgment of theirs.

al-Zajjaj said: "ma" is in the accusative position with the sense of "saa" (evil) being a thing or a judgment that they judge. He said: it is also permissible that "ma" be in the nominative position with the sense of "evil is the thing or the judgment, their judgment." Ibn Kaysan made it a verbal noun (masdariyyah), meaning "evil is their judgment."

﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah﴾: that is, whoever hopes. "Raja'" (hope) here means "tama'" (longing). Said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr. It was also said that "raja'" here means fear. al-Qurtubi said: the people of tafsir agreed that the meaning is, "whoever fears death." From this is the verse of al-Hudhali:

"When the hornet stings him, he does not hope for its sting."

al-Zajjaj said: the meaning of "whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah" is: whoever hopes for the reward of the meeting with Allah, that is, the reward of arriving at Him. So "raja'" in this sense means hope. ﴿Then indeed the term of Allah is coming﴾, that is, the term set for the resurrection is coming without doubt. Muqatil said: it means the Day of Resurrection, and the meaning is: let him work for that day, as in His words: ﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous work﴾ [al-Kahf: 110]. The "man" in this verse may be conditional, with the answer being "indeed the term of Allah is coming." It may also be relative, and the "fa" has entered its response, likening it to the conditional.

In the verse there is promise, warning, intimidation and encouragement that is evident. He is the All-Hearing of the words of His servants, the All-Knowing of what they conceal and what they make public.

﴿Whoever strives, he strives only for himself﴾: that is, whoever strives against the disbelievers and strives against his own self through patience in acts of obedience, he strives only for himself, that is, the reward of that is for him and not for another, and nothing of its benefit returns to Allah, glory be to Him. ﴿Indeed Allah is Free of need from the worlds﴾, so He has no need of their obedience, just as their disobedience does not harm Him.

It was also said: the meaning is that whoever strives against his enemy for his own sake, not seeking thereby the face of Allah, then Allah has no need of his striving. The first is preferable.

﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds – We will surely remove from them their misdeeds﴾: that is, We will cover them over for them with forgiveness because of the righteous deeds they did. ﴿And We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do﴾: that is, with the best reward for their deeds. It was also said: with the reward for the best of their deeds. The intent of "best" is merely the description and not the comparative, lest their reward for goodness be left unmentioned. It was also said: He gives them more than what they did and better than it, as in His words: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed, for him is ten times its like﴾ [al-An'am: 160].

﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents﴾: the accusative of "husnan" is as a qualifier of an omitted verbal noun, that is, an enjoining that is good, for emphasis, or by omitting the genitive: that is, possessing goodness.

This is the position of the Basrans. The Kufans said: its estimate is "We enjoined upon man that he do good," so it is an object of an omitted verb. From this is the poet's saying:

"I wondered at Dahmaa when she complains about us,
And at Abu Dahmaa when he advises us to do good to her, as if they feared us."

That is, he advises us that we should do good to her. Similar is the saying of al-Hutay'ah:

"I have advised the free heart of Barrah: good to the dog and evil to the mother-in-law."

al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is, "We enjoined upon man": that he should do toward his parents what is good. It was also said: it is a qualifier of an omitted noun, that is, "We enjoined upon him a matter that is good." It was also said: it is in the accusative position as an object by implicit transitivity (tadmin), meaning "We obligated him to goodness." It was also said: it is in the accusative by removal of the preposition, meaning "We enjoined him with goodness." It was also said: it is a verbal noun of an omitted verb, meaning "he is good, goodness." The meaning of the verse is: the charge to man concerning his parents, to be dutiful to them and to be kind to them.

The majority read "husnan" with a damma on the ha and sukun on the mim. Abu al-Rajaa, Abu al-Aliyah and al-Dahhak read it with fatha on both. al-Jahdari read "ihsanan," and so also in the Mushaf of Ubayy.

﴿And if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them﴾: that is, they ask you and compel you to associate with Me a god of which you have no knowledge that it is a god. So do not obey them. Indeed "there is no obedience to a created being in disobedience to the Creator." He expressed the negation of knowledge in place of the negation of divinity, because what its soundness is not known for, it is not permissible to follow, so how about what is known to be false? And if obedience to the two parents is not permissible in this demand, even with their striving upon him, then its impermissibility with mere demand without striving from them is more fitting. Attached to the request for association from them is all the disobedience of Allah, glory be to Him. So there is no obedience to them in what is disobedience to Allah, as has been authentically reported from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). ﴿To Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do﴾: that is, I will inform you of your good deeds and your bad deeds, and then I will reward each of you according to what he deserves.

The relative pronoun in His words "those who believe and do righteous deeds" is in the nominative position as the subject, and its predicate is ﴿We will surely admit them among the righteous﴾: that is, into the company of those firmly established in righteousness. It is permissible that it be in the accusative position by way of preoccupation (ishtighal). It is permissible that the meaning be: "We will surely admit them into the place of entry of the righteous," which is Paradise, as it was said. The first is preferable.

﴿And among the people is he who says, "We believe in Allah," but when he is harmed for the sake of Allah﴾: that is, in the matter of Allah and for His sake, as the people of disbelief do with the people of faith, and as the people of sin do with the people of obedience, by inflicting harm upon them for the sake of faith in Allah and acting upon what He commanded. ﴿He regards the trial of people﴾, which is what they inflict upon him of harm, ﴿as like the punishment of Allah﴾: that is, he became distressed by their harm, did not endure it, and made it in severity and magnitude like the punishment of Allah, so he obeyed the people as he obeys Allah. It was also said: this is the hypocrite, who when he is harmed for the sake of Allah turns back from the religion and disbelieves.

al-Zajjaj said: it is fitting for the believer to endure harm for the sake of Allah. ﴿But if victory comes from your Lord﴾: that is, victory from Allah for the believers, conquest and triumph over the enemies, and spoils that they gain from them. ﴿They will surely say, "Indeed we were with you"﴾: that is, we are entering with you into your religion and helping you against your enemy. So Allah refutes them and says: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of what is within the breasts of the worlds?﴾: that is, He, glory be to Him, is most knowing of what is in their breasts, of good and evil from them, so how do they make this false claim?

These are a people from among those whose faith was weak. When harm from the disbelievers touched them, they went along with them. And when the strength of Islam appeared and Allah gave victory to the believers in some battle, they said, "Indeed we were with you." It was also said: what is meant by this and what precedes it is the hypocrites.

Mujahid said: it was revealed concerning people who believed in Allah with their tongues. So when a trial from Allah or a calamity befell them, they were seduced.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 29, verses 2–13 (part 2 of 2):

al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: It was revealed concerning some hypocrites in Mecca who would profess faith, but when they were harmed they reverted to polytheism. The apparent reading is that this arrangement, from His saying "And among the people is he who says" up to His saying "And those who disbelieved said," was revealed concerning the hypocrites, because this is what the context makes apparent.

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah will surely know those who have believed, and He will surely know the hypocrites﴾, it is there to confirm and reinforce what precedes it. That is: Allah will surely distinguish between the two groups, and the sincerity of the sincere and the hypocrisy of the hypocrites will become manifest. The sincere believer is one who is not shaken by the harm that befalls him, who is patient for the sake of Allah with the patience due to Him, and who does not make the trial by people equal to the punishment of Allah.

The hypocrite, however, inclines this way and that. If harm from the disbelievers befalls him, he goes along with them, follows them, and disbelieves in Allah, Mighty and Majestic. But if the breeze of Islam blows (in his favor), his victory appears and his conquest shines forth, he returns to Islam and claims that he is among the Muslims.

(p-1115) ﴿And those who disbelieved said to those who believed, "Follow our way, and we will bear your sins."﴾ The lām in ﴿lilladhīna āmanū﴾ (to those who believed) is the lām of conveyance (lām al-tablīgh), meaning that they spoke to them directly, as has been explained in more than one place. That is: they said to them, "Take our path and enter into our religion." ﴿And we will bear your sins﴾: that is, if following our way is a sin for which you will be held to account at the resurrection and the gathering, as you claim, then let us bear that on your behalf and be held to account for it instead of you. The lām in ﴿wa-l-naḥmil﴾ (and let us bear) is the lām of command, as though they were commanding themselves to do so.

al-Farrā' and al-Zajjāj said: It is an imperative in the sense of a conditional and its consequence. That is: "If you follow our way, we will bear your sins." Then Allah answered them with His saying: ﴿But they will not bear anything of their sins﴾. The first ﴿min﴾ (of ﴿min khaṭāyāhum﴾) is explanatory (bayāniyya), and the second is extra (zā'ida) for generality (li-l-istighrāq): that is, they will not bear any part whatsoever of their sins, which they had obligated themselves to and guaranteed to bear for them. Then Allah, Glorified is He, described them with lying in this undertaking to bear the burden, saying: ﴿Indeed, they are liars in what they guaranteed of bearing your sins﴾.

al-Mahdawī said: This denial from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, was construed according to the meaning, because the meaning is: "If you follow our way, we will bear your sins." Since the command, in meaning, reverts to a statement of fact, the denial was applied to it, just as denial is applied to a statement of fact.

﴿And they will surely bear their own burdens﴾: that is, their wrongs which they committed. The expression of them as "burdens" indicates that they are great sins. ﴿And burdens along with their burdens﴾: that is, wrongs along with their wrongs. These are the wrongs of those whom they misled and drew away from guidance into error. Similar to this is His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿That they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and also some of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge﴾ [al-Naḥl: 25]. Similar to this is the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Whoever establishes an evil practice in Islam, upon him is its burden and the burden of whoever acts upon it," as in the hadith of Abū Hurayrah which is authentic in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim and elsewhere.

﴿And they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection﴾ as a rebuke and reproach, ﴿concerning what they used to fabricate﴾: that is, what they invented of lies which they used to bring forth in the world.

Muqātil said: It refers to their saying, "We are the guarantors for every consequence that befalls you from Allah."

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted, concerning His saying: ﴿Alif-Lām-Mīm. Do the people think that they will be left⦆ to the end of the verse, that he said: It was revealed concerning some people in Mecca who had professed Islam. The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Medina wrote to them when the verse of emigration was revealed, that no profession or Islam would be accepted from them until they emigrated. He said: So they set out intending to go to Medina, but the polytheists pursued them and turned them back. Then this verse was revealed concerning them. They wrote to them that such-and-such had been revealed concerning them. They said: "We will go out, and if anyone follows us, we will kill him." So they went out, the polytheists pursued them, and they fought them. Some of them were killed and some escaped. Then Allah revealed concerning them: ﴿Then indeed your Lord — for those who emigrated after they had been tried, then struggled and were patient — indeed your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Naḥl: 110].

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted similarly from Qatādah, more briefly. Ibn Saʿd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Ibn ʿAsākir transmitted from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmayr who said: It was revealed concerning ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir when he was being tortured for the sake of Allah: ﴿Alif-Lām-Mīm. Do the people think that they will be left⦆ to the end of the verse.

Ibn Mājah and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn Masʿūd who said: The first whose Islam Allah made manifest were seven: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Abū Bakr, Sumayyah the mother of ʿAmmār, ʿAmmār, Ṣuhayb, Bilāl and al-Miqdād.

As for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Allah protected him through his uncle Abū Ṭālib; as for Abū Bakr, Allah protected him through his people; as for the rest, the polytheists seized them, put coats of iron mail on them and exposed them to the sun. There was not one of them but that he had complied with what they wanted, except Bilāl, for his soul was made light to him for the sake of Allah, and he was held lightly by his people. So they seized him and gave him to the boys, and they began to drag him around the valleys of Mecca while he kept saying: "One! One!"

al-Firyābī, Ibn Abī Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Mujāhid concerning His saying ﴿that they could outrun us﴾ that he said: that they could overpower us.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ who said: My mother said, "I will not eat any food or drink any drink until you disbelieve in Muḥammad." She refrained from food and drink until they began to force her mouth open with a stick. Then this verse was revealed: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents; but if they strive to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them﴾.

al-Tirmidhī also transmitted this from him, and said: "Four verses were revealed concerning me," and he mentioned something similar to this story, and said: "Ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ."

Aḥmad, Muslim, Abū Dāwūd and al-Nasā'ī also transmitted this hadith.

Aḥmad, Ibn Abī Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, al-Tirmidhī (who graded it ṣaḥīḥ), Ibn Mājah, Abū Yaʿlā, Ibn Ḥibbān, Abū Nuʿaym, al-Bayhaqī and al-Ḍiyāʾ transmitted from Anas who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I was harmed for the sake of Allah, and no one is harmed as I am; I was frightened for the sake of Allah, and no one is frightened as I am. Three nights passed over me when I and Bilāl had no food that any living thing could eat, except what was concealed under Bilāl's armpit."

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His saying: ﴿He makes the trial of people equal to the punishment of Allah﴾ that he said: He apostatizes from the religion of Allah when he is harmed for the sake of Allah.

The surah is disputed as Meccan or Medinan, or partly one and partly the other, on three opinions. The first is that it is entirely Meccan, related by Ibn al-Duraysi, al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il from Ibn Abbas. Ibn Mardawayh also related it from Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, and this is the view of al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Ata' and Jabir ibn Zayd. The second is that it is entirely Medinan. al-Qurtubi said this is one of two opinions of Ibn Abbas and of Qatadah. The third is that it is Meccan except for its first ten verses. al-Qurtubi said this is the other opinion of Ibn Abbas and Qatadah, and it is the view of Yahya ibn Sallam. It is also reported from Ali ibn Abi Talib that it was revealed between Mecca and Medina, which is a fourth opinion.

al-Daraqutni related in al-Sunan from Aisha that "the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would pray at the eclipse of the sun and the moon four bowings and four prostrations, reciting in the first rak'ah al-Ankabut or al-Rum, and in the second Ya-Sin."

﴿Alif Lam Mim.﴾ ﴿Do people think that they will be left to say, "We believe," and that they will not be tested?﴾ ﴿Indeed We tested those before them, and Allah will surely know those who are truthful, and He will surely know the liars.﴾ ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that they will outrun Us? Evil is what they judge.﴾ ﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah, indeed the term of Allah is coming, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ ﴿And whoever strives, he strives only for himself. Indeed Allah is Free of need from the worlds.﴾ ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will surely remove from them their misdeeds and We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do.﴾ ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents, but if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them. To Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do.﴾ ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds – We will surely admit them among the righteous.﴾ ﴿And among the people is he who says, "We believe in Allah," but when he is harmed for the sake of Allah, he regards the trial of people as like the punishment of Allah. But if victory comes from your Lord, they will surely say, "Indeed we were with you." Is not Allah most knowing of what is within the breasts of the worlds?﴾ ﴿And Allah will surely make evident those who believe, and He will surely make evident the hypocrites.﴾ ﴿And those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Follow our way, and we will bear your sins," but they will not bear anything of their sins. Indeed they are liars.﴾ ﴿And they will surely bear their burdens and burdens along with their burdens, and they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to fabricate.﴾

The discussion of the opening of this surah has already been given in full in Surat al-Baqarah. The interrogative in His words ﴿Do people think﴾ is for rebuke and reproach. ﴿That they will be left﴾ is in the accusative position governed by "hasiba" (thought). The phrase "hasiba" together with what follows it stands in place of the two objects, according to Sibawayh and the majority. ﴿That they will say, "We believe"﴾ is in the accusative position, with the sense of "li-an yaqulu" (so that they say), or "bi-an yaqulu" (by saying), or "ʿala an yaqulu" (on the condition that they say). It was also said that it is a substitute (badal) for "that they will be left." The meaning of the verse is that people are not left without being tested or tried, ﴿while they are not tested﴾, that is, they are not tried in their wealth and their selves. The matter is not as they thought. Rather, He must test them until the sincere is distinguished from the hypocrite and the truthful from the liar. The verse is therefore brought to deny that supposition and to show it to be far-fetched, and to make clear that testing by various kinds of obligations and other things is necessary.

al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is, "Did they think that We would be content with them saying only that they are believers and not be examined by that which makes the reality of their faith evident?" This is His words: ﴿that they will be left to say, "We believe," and that they will not be tested.﴾

al-Suddi, Qatadah and Mujahid said: that is, they will not be tried in their wealth and their selves through killing and torment. The explanation of the cause of revelation of these verses, which will come, clarifies the meaning of what we have mentioned. The apparent sense of the verses includes all people among the believers. Even if the cause is specific, the consideration is the generality of the wording, as we have established more than once.

He said: it is also permissible that "ma" be in the nominative position with the sense of "evil is the thing or the judgment, their judgment." "I wondered at Dahmaa when she complains about us,
And at Abu Dahmaa when he advises us to do good to her, as if they feared us."

It was also said: it is a verbal noun of an omitted verb, meaning "he is good, goodness." The meaning of the verse is: the charge to man concerning his parents, to be dutiful to them and to be kind to them.

The majority read "husnan" with a damma on the ha and sukun on the mim. Abu al-Rajaa, Abu al-Aliyah and al-Dahhak read it with fatha on both. al-Jahdari read "ihsanan," and so also in the Mushaf of Ubayy.

﴿And if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them﴾: that is, they ask you and compel you to associate with Me a god of which you have no knowledge that it is a god. So do not obey them. Indeed "there is no obedience to a created being in disobedience to the Creator." He expressed the negation of knowledge in place of the negation of divinity, because what its soundness is not known for, it is not permissible to follow, so how about what is known to be false? And if obedience to the two parents is not permissible in this demand, even with their striving upon him, then its impermissibility with mere demand without striving from them is more fitting. Attached to the request for association from them is all the disobedience of Allah, glory be to Him. So there is no obedience to them in what is disobedience to Allah, as has been authentically reported from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). ﴿To Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do﴾: that is, I will inform you of your good deeds and your bad deeds, and then I will reward each of you according to what he deserves.

The relative pronoun in His words "those who believe and do righteous deeds" is in the nominative position as the subject, and its predicate is ﴿We will surely admit them among the righteous﴾: that is, into the company of those firmly established in righteousness. It is permissible that it be in the accusative position by way of preoccupation (ishtighal). It is permissible that the meaning be: "We will surely admit them into the place of entry of the righteous," which is Paradise, as it was said. The first is preferable.

﴿And among the people is he who says, "We believe in Allah," but when he is harmed for the sake of Allah﴾: that is, in the matter of Allah and for His sake, as the people of disbelief do with the people of faith, and as the people of sin do with the people of obedience, by inflicting harm upon them for the sake of faith in Allah and acting upon what He commanded. ﴿He regards the trial of people﴾, which is what they inflict upon him of harm, ﴿as like the punishment of Allah﴾: that is, he became distressed by their harm, did not endure it, and made it in severity and magnitude like the punishment of Allah, so he obeyed the people as he obeys Allah. It was also said: this is the hypocrite, who when he is harmed for the sake of Allah turns back from the religion and disbelieves.

al-Zajjaj said: it is fitting for the believer to endure harm for the sake of Allah. ﴿But if victory comes from your Lord﴾: that is, victory from Allah for the believers, conquest and triumph over the enemies, and spoils that they gain from them. ﴿They will surely say, "Indeed we were with you"﴾: that is, we are entering with you into your religion and helping you against your enemy. So Allah refutes them and says: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of what is within the breasts of the worlds?﴾: that is, He, glory be to Him, is most knowing of what is in their breasts, of good and evil from them, so how do they make this false claim?

These are a people from among those whose faith was weak. When harm from the disbelievers touched them, they went along with them. And when the strength of Islam appeared and Allah gave victory to the believers in some battle, they said, "Indeed we were with you." It was also said: what is meant by this and what precedes it is the hypocrites.

Mujahid said: it was revealed concerning people who believed in Allah with their tongues. So when a trial from Allah or a calamity befell them, they were seduced.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 29, verses 2–13 (part 2 of 2):

al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: It was revealed concerning some hypocrites in Mecca who would profess faith, but when they were harmed they reverted to polytheism. The apparent reading is that this arrangement, from His saying "And among the people is he who says" up to His saying "And those who disbelieved said," was revealed concerning the hypocrites, because this is what the context makes apparent.

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah will surely know those who have believed, and He will surely know the hypocrites﴾, it is there to confirm and reinforce what precedes it. That is: Allah will surely distinguish between the two groups, and the sincerity of the sincere and the hypocrisy of the hypocrites will become manifest. The sincere believer is one who is not shaken by the harm that befalls him, who is patient for the sake of Allah with the patience due to Him, and who does not make the trial by people equal to the punishment of Allah.

The hypocrite, however, inclines this way and that. If harm from the disbelievers befalls him, he goes along with them, follows them, and disbelieves in Allah, Mighty and Majestic. But if the breeze of Islam blows (in his favor), his victory appears and his conquest shines forth, he returns to Islam and claims that he is among the Muslims.

(p-1115) ﴿And those who disbelieved said to those who believed, "Follow our way, and we will bear your sins."﴾ The lām in ﴿lilladhīna āmanū﴾ (to those who believed) is the lām of conveyance (lām al-tablīgh), meaning that they spoke to them directly, as has been explained in more than one place. That is: they said to them, "Take our path and enter into our religion." ﴿And we will bear your sins﴾: that is, if following our way is a sin for which you will be held to account at the resurrection and the gathering, as you claim, then let us bear that on your behalf and be held to account for it instead of you. The lām in ﴿wa-l-naḥmil﴾ (and let us bear) is the lām of command, as though they were commanding themselves to do so.

al-Farrā' and al-Zajjāj said: It is an imperative in the sense of a conditional and its consequence. That is: "If you follow our way, we will bear your sins." Then Allah answered them with His saying: ﴿But they will not bear anything of their sins﴾. The first ﴿min﴾ (of ﴿min khaṭāyāhum﴾) is explanatory (bayāniyya), and the second is extra (zā'ida) for generality (li-l-istighrāq): that is, they will not bear any part whatsoever of their sins, which they had obligated themselves to and guaranteed to bear for them. Then Allah, Glorified is He, described them with lying in this undertaking to bear the burden, saying: ﴿Indeed, they are liars in what they guaranteed of bearing your sins﴾.

al-Mahdawī said: This denial from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, was construed according to the meaning, because the meaning is: "If you follow our way, we will bear your sins." Since the command, in meaning, reverts to a statement of fact, the denial was applied to it, just as denial is applied to a statement of fact.

﴿And they will surely bear their own burdens﴾: that is, their wrongs which they committed. The expression of them as "burdens" indicates that they are great sins. ﴿And burdens along with their burdens﴾: that is, wrongs along with their wrongs. These are the wrongs of those whom they misled and drew away from guidance into error. Similar to this is His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿That they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and also some of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge﴾ [al-Naḥl: 25]. Similar to this is the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Whoever establishes an evil practice in Islam, upon him is its burden and the burden of whoever acts upon it," as in the hadith of Abū Hurayrah which is authentic in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim and elsewhere.

﴿And they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection﴾ as a rebuke and reproach, ﴿concerning what they used to fabricate﴾: that is, what they invented of lies which they used to bring forth in the world.

Muqātil said: It refers to their saying, "We are the guarantors for every consequence that befalls you from Allah."

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted, concerning His saying: ﴿Alif-Lām-Mīm. Do the people think that they will be left⦆ to the end of the verse, that he said: It was revealed concerning some people in Mecca who had professed Islam. The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Medina wrote to them when the verse of emigration was revealed, that no profession or Islam would be accepted from them until they emigrated. He said: So they set out intending to go to Medina, but the polytheists pursued them and turned them back. Then this verse was revealed concerning them. They wrote to them that such-and-such had been revealed concerning them. They said: "We will go out, and if anyone follows us, we will kill him." So they went out, the polytheists pursued them, and they fought them. Some of them were killed and some escaped. Then Allah revealed concerning them: ﴿Then indeed your Lord — for those who emigrated after they had been tried, then struggled and were patient — indeed your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Naḥl: 110].

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted similarly from Qatādah, more briefly. Ibn Saʿd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Ibn ʿAsākir transmitted from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmayr who said: It was revealed concerning ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir when he was being tortured for the sake of Allah: ﴿Alif-Lām-Mīm. Do the people think that they will be left⦆ to the end of the verse.

Ibn Mājah and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn Masʿūd who said: The first whose Islam Allah made manifest were seven: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Abū Bakr, Sumayyah the mother of ʿAmmār, ʿAmmār, Ṣuhayb, Bilāl and al-Miqdād.

As for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Allah protected him through his uncle Abū Ṭālib; as for Abū Bakr, Allah protected him through his people; as for the rest, the polytheists seized them, put coats of iron mail on them and exposed them to the sun. There was not one of them but that he had complied with what they wanted, except Bilāl, for his soul was made light to him for the sake of Allah, and he was held lightly by his people. So they seized him and gave him to the boys, and they began to drag him around the valleys of Mecca while he kept saying: "One! One!"

al-Firyābī, Ibn Abī Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Mujāhid concerning His saying ﴿that they could outrun us﴾ that he said: that they could overpower us.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ who said: My mother said, "I will not eat any food or drink any drink until you disbelieve in Muḥammad." She refrained from food and drink until they began to force her mouth open with a stick. Then this verse was revealed: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents; but if they strive to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them﴾.

al-Tirmidhī also transmitted this from him, and said: "Four verses were revealed concerning me," and he mentioned something similar to this story, and said: "Ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ."

Aḥmad, Muslim, Abū Dāwūd and al-Nasā'ī also transmitted this hadith.

Aḥmad, Ibn Abī Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, al-Tirmidhī (who graded it ṣaḥīḥ), Ibn Mājah, Abū Yaʿlā, Ibn Ḥibbān, Abū Nuʿaym, al-Bayhaqī and al-Ḍiyāʾ transmitted from Anas who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I was harmed for the sake of Allah, and no one is harmed as I am; I was frightened for the sake of Allah, and no one is frightened as I am. Three nights passed over me when I and Bilāl had no food that any living thing could eat, except what was concealed under Bilāl's armpit."

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His saying: ﴿He makes the trial of people equal to the punishment of Allah﴾ that he said: He apostatizes from the religion of Allah when he is harmed for the sake of Allah.

The surah is disputed as Meccan or Medinan, or partly one and partly the other, on three opinions. The first is that it is entirely Meccan, related by Ibn al-Duraysi, al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il from Ibn Abbas. Ibn Mardawayh also related it from Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, and this is the view of al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Ata' and Jabir ibn Zayd. The second is that it is entirely Medinan. al-Qurtubi said this is one of two opinions of Ibn Abbas and of Qatadah. The third is that it is Meccan except for its first ten verses. al-Qurtubi said this is the other opinion of Ibn Abbas and Qatadah, and it is the view of Yahya ibn Sallam. It is also reported from Ali ibn Abi Talib that it was revealed between Mecca and Medina, which is a fourth opinion.

al-Daraqutni related in al-Sunan from Aisha that "the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would pray at the eclipse of the sun and the moon four bowings and four prostrations, reciting in the first rak'ah al-Ankabut or al-Rum, and in the second Ya-Sin."

﴿Alif Lam Mim.﴾ ﴿Do people think that they will be left to say, "We believe," and that they will not be tested?﴾ ﴿Indeed We tested those before them, and Allah will surely know those who are truthful, and He will surely know the liars.﴾ ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that they will outrun Us? Evil is what they judge.﴾ ﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah, indeed the term of Allah is coming, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ ﴿And whoever strives, he strives only for himself. Indeed Allah is Free of need from the worlds.﴾ ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will surely remove from them their misdeeds and We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do.﴾ ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents, but if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them. To Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do.﴾ ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds – We will surely admit them among the righteous.﴾ ﴿And among the people is he who says, "We believe in Allah," but when he is harmed for the sake of Allah, he regards the trial of people as like the punishment of Allah. But if victory comes from your Lord, they will surely say, "Indeed we were with you." Is not Allah most knowing of what is within the breasts of the worlds?﴾ ﴿And Allah will surely make evident those who believe, and He will surely make evident the hypocrites.﴾ ﴿And those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Follow our way, and we will bear your sins," but they will not bear anything of their sins. Indeed they are liars.﴾ ﴿And they will surely bear their burdens and burdens along with their burdens, and they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to fabricate.﴾

The discussion of the opening of this surah has already been given in full in Surat al-Baqarah. The interrogative in His words ﴿Do people think﴾ is for rebuke and reproach. ﴿That they will be left﴾ is in the accusative position governed by "hasiba" (thought). The phrase "hasiba" together with what follows it stands in place of the two objects, according to Sibawayh and the majority. ﴿That they will say, "We believe"﴾ is in the accusative position, with the sense of "li-an yaqulu" (so that they say), or "bi-an yaqulu" (by saying), or "ʿala an yaqulu" (on the condition that they say). It was also said that it is a substitute (badal) for "that they will be left." The meaning of the verse is that people are not left without being tested or tried, ﴿while they are not tested﴾, that is, they are not tried in their wealth and their selves. The matter is not as they thought. Rather, He must test them until the sincere is distinguished from the hypocrite and the truthful from the liar. The verse is therefore brought to deny that supposition and to show it to be far-fetched, and to make clear that testing by various kinds of obligations and other things is necessary.

al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is, "Did they think that We would be content with them saying only that they are believers and not be examined by that which makes the reality of their faith evident?" This is His words: ﴿that they will be left to say, "We believe," and that they will not be tested.﴾

al-Suddi, Qatadah and Mujahid said: that is, they will not be tried in their wealth and their selves through killing and torment. The explanation of the cause of revelation of these verses, which will come, clarifies the meaning of what we have mentioned. The apparent sense of the verses includes all people among the believers. Even if the cause is specific, the consideration is the generality of the wording, as we have established more than once.

Ibn Atiyyah said: although this verse was revealed concerning a specific cause, its ruling remains in the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) and is operative for the rest of time, because the trial from Allah continues on the frontiers of the Muslims through captivity, the attacks of the enemy, and other things.

﴿Indeed We tested those before them﴾: that is, this is the way of Allah with His servants, that He tests the believers of this community just as He tested those nations before them. This is what the Qur'an has brought in more than one place concerning the stories of the prophets, and what befell them and their peoples of trials, and what Allah tested their followers and those who believed in them with, of those matters that befell them. ﴿Allah will surely know those who are truthful﴾ in their saying, "We believe," ﴿and He will surely know the liars﴾ among them in that. The majority read "fa-la-yaʿlamanna" with a fatha on the ya and the lam in both places, meaning that Allah will make manifest the truthful and the liar in their saying and will distinguish between them. ʿAli ibn Abi Talib read it in both places with a damma on the ya and a kasra on the lam.

The meaning: that is, He will inform the two groups in the Hereafter of their stations, or He will inform the people of the truthfulness of the truthful and expose the liars for their lying, or He will assign to each group a sign by which it becomes known and distinguished from others.

﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that they will outrun Us?﴾ that is, they will escape and overcome Us before We call them to account for what they do. This clause takes the place of the two objects of "hasiba." "Am" here is the disjunctive (munqati'ah) "am." ﴿Evil is what they judge﴾, that is, wretched is what they judge, that judgment of theirs.

al-Zajjaj said: "ma" is in the accusative position with the sense of "saa" (evil) being a thing or a judgment that they judge. He said: it is also permissible that "ma" be in the nominative position with the sense of "evil is the thing or the judgment, their judgment." Ibn Kaysan made it a verbal noun (masdariyyah), meaning "evil is their judgment."

﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah﴾: that is, whoever hopes. "Raja'" (hope) here means "tama'" (longing). Said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr. It was also said that "raja'" here means fear. al-Qurtubi said: the people of tafsir agreed that the meaning is, "whoever fears death." From this is the verse of al-Hudhali:

"When the hornet stings him, he does not hope for its sting."

al-Zajjaj said: the meaning of "whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah" is: whoever hopes for the reward of the meeting with Allah, that is, the reward of arriving at Him. So "raja'" in this sense means hope. ﴿Then indeed the term of Allah is coming﴾, that is, the term set for the resurrection is coming without doubt. Muqatil said: it means the Day of Resurrection, and the meaning is: let him work for that day, as in His words: ﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous work﴾ [al-Kahf: 110]. The "man" in this verse may be conditional, with the answer being "indeed the term of Allah is coming." It may also be relative, and the "fa" has entered its response, likening it to the conditional.

In the verse there is promise, warning, intimidation and encouragement that is evident. He is the All-Hearing of the words of His servants, the All-Knowing of what they conceal and what they make public.

﴿Whoever strives, he strives only for himself﴾: that is, whoever strives against the disbelievers and strives against his own self through patience in acts of obedience, he strives only for himself, that is, the reward of that is for him and not for another, and nothing of its benefit returns to Allah, glory be to Him. ﴿Indeed Allah is Free of need from the worlds﴾, so He has no need of their obedience, just as their disobedience does not harm Him.

It was also said: the meaning is that whoever strives against his enemy for his own sake, not seeking thereby the face of Allah, then Allah has no need of his striving. The first is preferable.

﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds – We will surely remove from them their misdeeds﴾: that is, We will cover them over for them with forgiveness because of the righteous deeds they did. ﴿And We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do﴾: that is, with the best reward for their deeds. It was also said: with the reward for the best of their deeds. The intent of "best" is merely the description and not the comparative, lest their reward for goodness be left unmentioned. It was also said: He gives them more than what they did and better than it, as in His words: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed, for him is ten times its like﴾ [al-An'am: 160].

﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents﴾: the accusative of "husnan" is as a qualifier of an omitted verbal noun, that is, an enjoining that is good, for emphasis, or by omitting the genitive: that is, possessing goodness.

This is the position of the Basrans. The Kufans said: its estimate is "We enjoined upon man that he do good," so it is an object of an omitted verb. From this is the poet's saying:

"I wondered at Dahmaa when she complains about us,
And at Abu Dahmaa when he advises us to do good to her, as if they feared us."

That is, he advises us that we should do good to her. Similar is the saying of al-Hutay'ah:

"I have advised the free heart of Barrah: good to the dog and evil to the mother-in-law."

al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is, "We enjoined upon man": that he should do toward his parents what is good. It was also said: it is a qualifier of an omitted noun, that is, "We enjoined upon him a matter that is good." It was also said: it is in the accusative position as an object by implicit transitivity (tadmin), meaning "We obligated him to goodness." It was also said: it is in the accusative by removal of the preposition, meaning "We enjoined him with goodness." It was also said: it is a verbal noun of an omitted verb, meaning "he is good, goodness." The meaning of the verse is: the charge to man concerning his parents, to be dutiful to them and to be kind to them.

The majority read "husnan" with a damma on the ha and sukun on the mim. Abu al-Rajaa, Abu al-Aliyah and al-Dahhak read it with fatha on both. al-Jahdari read "ihsanan," and so also in the Mushaf of Ubayy.

﴿And if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them﴾: that is, they ask you and compel you to associate with Me a god of which you have no knowledge that it is a god. So do not obey them. Indeed "there is no obedience to a created being in disobedience to the Creator." He expressed the negation of knowledge in place of the negation of divinity, because what its soundness is not known for, it is not permissible to follow, so how about what is known to be false? And if obedience to the two parents is not permissible in this demand, even with their striving upon him, then its impermissibility with mere demand without striving from them is more fitting. Attached to the request for association from them is all the disobedience of Allah, glory be to Him. So there is no obedience to them in what is disobedience to Allah, as has been authentically reported from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). ﴿To Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do﴾: that is, I will inform you of your good deeds and your bad deeds, and then I will reward each of you according to what he deserves.

The relative pronoun in His words "those who believe and do righteous deeds" is in the nominative position as the subject, and its predicate is ﴿We will surely admit them among the righteous﴾: that is, into the company of those firmly established in righteousness. It is permissible that it be in the accusative position by way of preoccupation (ishtighal). It is permissible that the meaning be: "We will surely admit them into the place of entry of the righteous," which is Paradise, as it was said. The first is preferable.

﴿And among the people is he who says, "We believe in Allah," but when he is harmed for the sake of Allah﴾: that is, in the matter of Allah and for His sake, as the people of disbelief do with the people of faith, and as the people of sin do with the people of obedience, by inflicting harm upon them for the sake of faith in Allah and acting upon what He commanded. ﴿He regards the trial of people﴾, which is what they inflict upon him of harm, ﴿as like the punishment of Allah﴾: that is, he became distressed by their harm, did not endure it, and made it in severity and magnitude like the punishment of Allah, so he obeyed the people as he obeys Allah. It was also said: this is the hypocrite, who when he is harmed for the sake of Allah turns back from the religion and disbelieves.

al-Zajjaj said: it is fitting for the believer to endure harm for the sake of Allah. ﴿But if victory comes from your Lord﴾: that is, victory from Allah for the believers, conquest and triumph over the enemies, and spoils that they gain from them. ﴿They will surely say, "Indeed we were with you"﴾: that is, we are entering with you into your religion and helping you against your enemy. So Allah refutes them and says: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of what is within the breasts of the worlds?﴾: that is, He, glory be to Him, is most knowing of what is in their breasts, of good and evil from them, so how do they make this false claim?

These are a people from among those whose faith was weak. When harm from the disbelievers touched them, they went along with them. And when the strength of Islam appeared and Allah gave victory to the believers in some battle, they said, "Indeed we were with you." It was also said: what is meant by this and what precedes it is the hypocrites.

Mujahid said: it was revealed concerning people who believed in Allah with their tongues. So when a trial from Allah or a calamity befell them, they were seduced.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 29, verses 2–13 (part 2 of 2):

Then Allah answered them with His saying: ﴿But they will not bear anything of their sins﴾. The first ﴿min﴾ (of ﴿min khaṭāyāhum﴾) is explanatory (bayāniyya), and the second is extra (zā'ida) for generality (li-l-istighrāq): that is, they will not bear any part whatsoever of their sins, which they had obligated themselves to and guaranteed to bear for them. Then Allah, Glorified is He, described them with lying in this undertaking to bear the burden, saying: ﴿Indeed, they are liars in what they guaranteed of bearing your sins﴾.

al-Mahdawī said: This denial from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, was construed according to the meaning, because the meaning is: "If you follow our way, we will bear your sins." Since the command, in meaning, reverts to a statement of fact, the denial was applied to it, just as denial is applied to a statement of fact.

﴿And they will surely bear their own burdens﴾: that is, their wrongs which they committed. The expression of them as "burdens" indicates that they are great sins. ﴿And burdens along with their burdens﴾: that is, wrongs along with their wrongs. These are the wrongs of those whom they misled and drew away from guidance into error. Similar to this is His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿That they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and also some of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge﴾ [al-Naḥl: 25]. Similar to this is the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Whoever establishes an evil practice in Islam, upon him is its burden and the burden of whoever acts upon it," as in the hadith of Abū Hurayrah which is authentic in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim and elsewhere.

﴿And they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection﴾ as a rebuke and reproach, ﴿concerning what they used to fabricate﴾: that is, what they invented of lies which they used to bring forth in the world.

Muqātil said: It refers to their saying, "We are the guarantors for every consequence that befalls you from Allah."

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted, concerning His saying: ﴿Alif-Lām-Mīm. Do the people think that they will be left⦆ to the end of the verse, that he said: It was revealed concerning some people in Mecca who had professed Islam. The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Medina wrote to them when the verse of emigration was revealed, that no profession or Islam would be accepted from them until they emigrated. He said: So they set out intending to go to Medina, but the polytheists pursued them and turned them back. Then this verse was revealed concerning them. They wrote to them that such-and-such had been revealed concerning them. They said: "We will go out, and if anyone follows us, we will kill him." So they went out, the polytheists pursued them, and they fought them. Some of them were killed and some escaped. Then Allah revealed concerning them: ﴿Then indeed your Lord — for those who emigrated after they had been tried, then struggled and were patient — indeed your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Naḥl: 110].

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted similarly from Qatādah, more briefly. Ibn Saʿd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Ibn ʿAsākir transmitted from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmayr who said: It was revealed concerning ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir when he was being tortured for the sake of Allah: ﴿Alif-Lām-Mīm. Do the people think that they will be left⦆ to the end of the verse.

Ibn Mājah and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn Masʿūd who said: The first whose Islam Allah made manifest were seven: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Abū Bakr, Sumayyah the mother of ʿAmmār, ʿAmmār, Ṣuhayb, Bilāl and al-Miqdād.

As for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Allah protected him through his uncle Abū Ṭālib; as for Abū Bakr, Allah protected him through his people; as for the rest, the polytheists seized them, put coats of iron mail on them and exposed them to the sun. There was not one of them but that he had complied with what they wanted, except Bilāl, for his soul was made light to him for the sake of Allah, and he was held lightly by his people. So they seized him and gave him to the boys, and they began to drag him around the valleys of Mecca while he kept saying: "One! One!"

al-Firyābī, Ibn Abī Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Mujāhid concerning His saying ﴿that they could outrun us﴾ that he said: that they could overpower us.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ who said: My mother said, "I will not eat any food or drink any drink until you disbelieve in Muḥammad." She refrained from food and drink until they began to force her mouth open with a stick. Then this verse was revealed: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents; but if they strive to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them﴾.

al-Tirmidhī also transmitted this from him, and said: "Four verses were revealed concerning me," and he mentioned something similar to this story, and said: "Ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ."

Aḥmad, Muslim, Abū Dāwūd and al-Nasā'ī also transmitted this hadith.

Aḥmad, Ibn Abī Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, al-Tirmidhī (who graded it ṣaḥīḥ), Ibn Mājah, Abū Yaʿlā, Ibn Ḥibbān, Abū Nuʿaym, al-Bayhaqī and al-Ḍiyāʾ transmitted from Anas who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I was harmed for the sake of Allah, and no one is harmed as I am; I was frightened for the sake of Allah, and no one is frightened as I am. Three nights passed over me when I and Bilāl had no food that any living thing could eat, except what was concealed under Bilāl's armpit."

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His saying: ﴿He makes the trial of people equal to the punishment of Allah﴾ that he said: He apostatizes from the religion of Allah when he is harmed for the sake of Allah.

The surah is disputed as Meccan or Medinan, or partly one and partly the other, on three opinions. The first is that it is entirely Meccan, related by Ibn al-Duraysi, al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il from Ibn Abbas. Ibn Mardawayh also related it from Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, and this is the view of al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Ata' and Jabir ibn Zayd. The second is that it is entirely Medinan. al-Qurtubi said this is one of two opinions of Ibn Abbas and of Qatadah. The third is that it is Meccan except for its first ten verses. al-Qurtubi said this is the other opinion of Ibn Abbas and Qatadah, and it is the view of Yahya ibn Sallam. It is also reported from Ali ibn Abi Talib that it was revealed between Mecca and Medina, which is a fourth opinion.

al-Daraqutni related in al-Sunan from Aisha that "the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would pray at the eclipse of the sun and the moon four bowings and four prostrations, reciting in the first rak'ah al-Ankabut or al-Rum, and in the second Ya-Sin."

﴿Alif Lam Mim.﴾ ﴿Do people think that they will be left to say, "We believe," and that they will not be tested?﴾ ﴿Indeed We tested those before them, and Allah will surely know those who are truthful, and He will surely know the liars.﴾ ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that they will outrun Us? Evil is what they judge.﴾ ﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah, indeed the term of Allah is coming, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ ﴿And whoever strives, he strives only for himself. Indeed Allah is Free of need from the worlds.﴾ ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will surely remove from them their misdeeds and We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do.﴾ ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents, but if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them. To Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do.﴾ ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds – We will surely admit them among the righteous.﴾ ﴿And among the people is he who says, "We believe in Allah," but when he is harmed for the sake of Allah, he regards the trial of people as like the punishment of Allah. But if victory comes from your Lord, they will surely say, "Indeed we were with you." Is not Allah most knowing of what is within the breasts of the worlds?﴾ ﴿And Allah will surely make evident those who believe, and He will surely make evident the hypocrites.﴾ ﴿And those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Follow our way, and we will bear your sins," but they will not bear anything of their sins. Indeed they are liars.﴾ ﴿And they will surely bear their burdens and burdens along with their burdens, and they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to fabricate.﴾

The discussion of the opening of this surah has already been given in full in Surat al-Baqarah. The interrogative in His words ﴿Do people think﴾ is for rebuke and reproach. ﴿That they will be left﴾ is in the accusative position governed by "hasiba" (thought). The phrase "hasiba" together with what follows it stands in place of the two objects, according to Sibawayh and the majority. ﴿That they will say, "We believe"﴾ is in the accusative position, with the sense of "li-an yaqulu" (so that they say), or "bi-an yaqulu" (by saying), or "ʿala an yaqulu" (on the condition that they say). It was also said that it is a substitute (badal) for "that they will be left." The meaning of the verse is that people are not left without being tested or tried, ﴿while they are not tested﴾, that is, they are not tried in their wealth and their selves. The matter is not as they thought. Rather, He must test them until the sincere is distinguished from the hypocrite and the truthful from the liar. The verse is therefore brought to deny that supposition and to show it to be far-fetched, and to make clear that testing by various kinds of obligations and other things is necessary.

al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is, "Did they think that We would be content with them saying only that they are believers and not be examined by that which makes the reality of their faith evident?" This is His words: ﴿that they will be left to say, "We believe," and that they will not be tested.﴾

al-Suddi, Qatadah and Mujahid said: that is, they will not be tried in their wealth and their selves through killing and torment. The explanation of the cause of revelation of these verses, which will come, clarifies the meaning of what we have mentioned. The apparent sense of the verses includes all people among the believers. Even if the cause is specific, the consideration is the generality of the wording, as we have established more than once.

Ibn Atiyyah said: although this verse was revealed concerning a specific cause, its ruling remains in the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) and is operative for the rest of time, because the trial from Allah continues on the frontiers of the Muslims through captivity, the attacks of the enemy, and other things.

﴿Indeed We tested those before them﴾: that is, this is the way of Allah with His servants, that He tests the believers of this community just as He tested those nations before them. This is what the Qur'an has brought in more than one place concerning the stories of the prophets, and what befell them and their peoples of trials, and what Allah tested their followers and those who believed in them with, of those matters that befell them. ﴿Allah will surely know those who are truthful﴾ in their saying, "We believe," ﴿and He will surely know the liars﴾ among them in that. The majority read "fa-la-yaʿlamanna" with a fatha on the ya and the lam in both places, meaning that Allah will make manifest the truthful and the liar in their saying and will distinguish between them. ʿAli ibn Abi Talib read it in both places with a damma on the ya and a kasra on the lam.

The meaning: that is, He will inform the two groups in the Hereafter of their stations, or He will inform the people of the truthfulness of the truthful and expose the liars for their lying, or He will assign to each group a sign by which it becomes known and distinguished from others.

﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that they will outrun Us?﴾ that is, they will escape and overcome Us before We call them to account for what they do. This clause takes the place of the two objects of "hasiba." "Am" here is the disjunctive (munqati'ah) "am." ﴿Evil is what they judge﴾, that is, wretched is what they judge, that judgment of theirs.

al-Zajjaj said: "ma" is in the accusative position with the sense of "saa" (evil) being a thing or a judgment that they judge. He said: it is also permissible that "ma" be in the nominative position with the sense of "evil is the thing or the judgment, their judgment." Ibn Kaysan made it a verbal noun (masdariyyah), meaning "evil is their judgment."

﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah﴾: that is, whoever hopes. "Raja'" (hope) here means "tama'" (longing). Said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr. It was also said that "raja'" here means fear. al-Qurtubi said: the people of tafsir agreed that the meaning is, "whoever fears death." From this is the verse of al-Hudhali:

"When the hornet stings him, he does not hope for its sting."

al-Zajjaj said: the meaning of "whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah" is: whoever hopes for the reward of the meeting with Allah, that is, the reward of arriving at Him. So "raja'" in this sense means hope. ﴿Then indeed the term of Allah is coming﴾, that is, the term set for the resurrection is coming without doubt. Muqatil said: it means the Day of Resurrection, and the meaning is: let him work for that day, as in His words: ﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous work﴾ [al-Kahf: 110]. The "man" in this verse may be conditional, with the answer being "indeed the term of Allah is coming." It may also be relative, and the "fa" has entered its response, likening it to the conditional.

In the verse there is promise, warning, intimidation and encouragement that is evident. He is the All-Hearing of the words of His servants, the All-Knowing of what they conceal and what they make public.

﴿Whoever strives, he strives only for himself﴾: that is, whoever strives against the disbelievers and strives against his own self through patience in acts of obedience, he strives only for himself, that is, the reward of that is for him and not for another, and nothing of its benefit returns to Allah, glory be to Him. ﴿Indeed Allah is Free of need from the worlds﴾, so He has no need of their obedience, just as their disobedience does not harm Him.

It was also said: the meaning is that whoever strives against his enemy for his own sake, not seeking thereby the face of Allah, then Allah has no need of his striving. The first is preferable.

﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds – We will surely remove from them their misdeeds﴾: that is, We will cover them over for them with forgiveness because of the righteous deeds they did. ﴿And We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do﴾: that is, with the best reward for their deeds. It was also said: with the reward for the best of their deeds. The intent of "best" is merely the description and not the comparative, lest their reward for goodness be left unmentioned. It was also said: He gives them more than what they did and better than it, as in His words: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed, for him is ten times its like﴾ [al-An'am: 160].

﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents﴾: the accusative of "husnan" is as a qualifier of an omitted verbal noun, that is, an enjoining that is good, for emphasis, or by omitting the genitive: that is, possessing goodness.

This is the position of the Basrans. The Kufans said: its estimate is "We enjoined upon man that he do good," so it is an object of an omitted verb. From this is the poet's saying:

"I wondered at Dahmaa when she complains about us,
And at Abu Dahmaa when he advises us to do good to her, as if they feared us."

That is, he advises us that we should do good to her. Similar is the saying of al-Hutay'ah:

"I have advised the free heart of Barrah: good to the dog and evil to the mother-in-law."

al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is, "We enjoined upon man": that he should do toward his parents what is good. It was also said: it is a qualifier of an omitted noun, that is, "We enjoined upon him a matter that is good." It was also said: it is in the accusative position as an object by implicit transitivity (tadmin), meaning "We obligated him to goodness." It was also said: it is in the accusative by removal of the preposition, meaning "We enjoined him with goodness." It was also said: it is a verbal noun of an omitted verb, meaning "he is good, goodness." The meaning of the verse is: the charge to man concerning his parents, to be dutiful to them and to be kind to them.

The majority read "husnan" with a damma on the ha and sukun on the mim. Abu al-Rajaa, Abu al-Aliyah and al-Dahhak read it with fatha on both. al-Jahdari read "ihsanan," and so also in the Mushaf of Ubayy.

﴿And if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them﴾: that is, they ask you and compel you to associate with Me a god of which you have no knowledge that it is a god. So do not obey them. Indeed "there is no obedience to a created being in disobedience to the Creator." He expressed the negation of knowledge in place of the negation of divinity, because what its soundness is not known for, it is not permissible to follow, so how about what is known to be false? And if obedience to the two parents is not permissible in this demand, even with their striving upon him, then its impermissibility with mere demand without striving from them is more fitting. Attached to the request for association from them is all the disobedience of Allah, glory be to Him. So there is no obedience to them in what is disobedience to Allah, as has been authentically reported from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). ﴿To Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do﴾: that is, I will inform you of your good deeds and your bad deeds, and then I will reward each of you according to what he deserves.

The relative pronoun in His words "those who believe and do righteous deeds" is in the nominative position as the subject, and its predicate is ﴿We will surely admit them among the righteous﴾: that is, into the company of those firmly established in righteousness. It is permissible that it be in the accusative position by way of preoccupation (ishtighal). It is permissible that the meaning be: "We will surely admit them into the place of entry of the righteous," which is Paradise, as it was said. The first is preferable.

﴿And among the people is he who says, "We believe in Allah," but when he is harmed for the sake of Allah﴾: that is, in the matter of Allah and for His sake, as the people of disbelief do with the people of faith, and as the people of sin do with the people of obedience, by inflicting harm upon them for the sake of faith in Allah and acting upon what He commanded. ﴿He regards the trial of people﴾, which is what they inflict upon him of harm, ﴿as like the punishment of Allah﴾: that is, he became distressed by their harm, did not endure it, and made it in severity and magnitude like the punishment of Allah, so he obeyed the people as he obeys Allah. It was also said: this is the hypocrite, who when he is harmed for the sake of Allah turns back from the religion and disbelieves.

al-Zajjaj said: it is fitting for the believer to endure harm for the sake of Allah. ﴿But if victory comes from your Lord﴾: that is, victory from Allah for the believers, conquest and triumph over the enemies, and spoils that they gain from them. ﴿They will surely say, "Indeed we were with you"﴾: that is, we are entering with you into your religion and helping you against your enemy. So Allah refutes them and says: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of what is within the breasts of the worlds?﴾: that is, He, glory be to Him, is most knowing of what is in their breasts, of good and evil from them, so how do they make this false claim?

These are a people from among those whose faith was weak. When harm from the disbelievers touched them, they went along with them. And when the strength of Islam appeared and Allah gave victory to the believers in some battle, they said, "Indeed we were with you." It was also said: what is meant by this and what precedes it is the hypocrites.

Mujahid said: it was revealed concerning people who believed in Allah with their tongues. So when a trial from Allah or a calamity befell them, they were seduced.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 29, verses 2–13 (part 2 of 2):

al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: It was revealed concerning some hypocrites in Mecca who would profess faith, but when they were harmed they reverted to polytheism. The apparent reading is that this arrangement, from His saying "And among the people is he who says" up to His saying "And those who disbelieved said," was revealed concerning the hypocrites, because this is what the context makes apparent.

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah will surely know those who have believed, and He will surely know the hypocrites﴾, it is there to confirm and reinforce what precedes it. That is: Allah will surely distinguish between the two groups, and the sincerity of the sincere and the hypocrisy of the hypocrites will become manifest. The sincere believer is one who is not shaken by the harm that befalls him, who is patient for the sake of Allah with the patience due to Him, and who does not make the trial by people equal to the punishment of Allah.

The hypocrite, however, inclines this way and that. If harm from the disbelievers befalls him, he goes along with them, follows them, and disbelieves in Allah, Mighty and Majestic. But if the breeze of Islam blows (in his favor), his victory appears and his conquest shines forth, he returns to Islam and claims that he is among the Muslims.

(p-1115) ﴿And those who disbelieved said to those who believed, "Follow our way, and we will bear your sins."﴾ The lām in ﴿lilladhīna āmanū﴾ (to those who believed) is the lām of conveyance (lām al-tablīgh), meaning that they spoke to them directly, as has been explained in more than one place. That is: they said to them, "Take our path and enter into our religion." ﴿And we will bear your sins﴾: that is, if following our way is a sin for which you will be held to account at the resurrection and the gathering, as you claim, then let us bear that on your behalf and be held to account for it instead of you. The lām in ﴿wa-l-naḥmil﴾ (and let us bear) is the lām of command, as though they were commanding themselves to do so.

al-Farrā' and al-Zajjāj said: It is an imperative in the sense of a conditional and its consequence. That is: "If you follow our way, we will bear your sins." Then Allah answered them with His saying: ﴿But they will not bear anything of their sins﴾. The first ﴿min﴾ (of ﴿min khaṭāyāhum﴾) is explanatory (bayāniyya), and the second is extra (zā'ida) for generality (li-l-istighrāq): that is, they will not bear any part whatsoever of their sins, which they had obligated themselves to and guaranteed to bear for them. Then Allah, Glorified is He, described them with lying in this undertaking to bear the burden, saying: ﴿Indeed, they are liars in what they guaranteed of bearing your sins﴾.

al-Mahdawī said: This denial from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, was construed according to the meaning, because the meaning is: "If you follow our way, we will bear your sins." Since the command, in meaning, reverts to a statement of fact, the denial was applied to it, just as denial is applied to a statement of fact.

﴿And they will surely bear their own burdens﴾: that is, their wrongs which they committed. The expression of them as "burdens" indicates that they are great sins. ﴿And burdens along with their burdens﴾: that is, wrongs along with their wrongs. These are the wrongs of those whom they misled and drew away from guidance into error. Similar to this is His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿That they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and also some of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge﴾ [al-Naḥl: 25]. Similar to this is the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Whoever establishes an evil practice in Islam, upon him is its burden and the burden of whoever acts upon it," as in the hadith of Abū Hurayrah which is authentic in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim and elsewhere.

﴿And they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection﴾ as a rebuke and reproach, ﴿concerning what they used to fabricate﴾: that is, what they invented of lies which they used to bring forth in the world.

Muqātil said: It refers to their saying, "We are the guarantors for every consequence that befalls you from Allah."

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted, concerning His saying: ﴿Alif-Lām-Mīm. Do the people think that they will be left⦆ to the end of the verse, that he said: It was revealed concerning some people in Mecca who had professed Islam. The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Medina wrote to them when the verse of emigration was revealed, that no profession or Islam would be accepted from them until they emigrated. He said: So they set out intending to go to Medina, but the polytheists pursued them and turned them back. Then this verse was revealed concerning them. They wrote to them that such-and-such had been revealed concerning them. They said: "We will go out, and if anyone follows us, we will kill him." So they went out, the polytheists pursued them, and they fought them. Some of them were killed and some escaped. Then Allah revealed concerning them: ﴿Then indeed your Lord — for those who emigrated after they had been tried, then struggled and were patient — indeed your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Naḥl: 110].

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted similarly from Qatādah, more briefly. Ibn Saʿd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Ibn ʿAsākir transmitted from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmayr who said: It was revealed concerning ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir when he was being tortured for the sake of Allah: ﴿Alif-Lām-Mīm. Do the people think that they will be left⦆ to the end of the verse.

So they seized him and gave him to the boys, and they began to drag him around the valleys of Mecca while he kept saying: "One! One!"
