Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him regarding His saying: ﴿And do not argue with the People of the Book except in a way that is best﴾ that he said: "[It is] 'There is no god but Allah.'"

al-Bukhari, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "The People of the Book used to recite the Torah in Hebrew and explain it to the People of Islam in Arabic. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Do not believe the People of the Book, nor disbelieve them, but say: We believe in what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to you, and our God and your God is One, and to Him we are submitting.'"

al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab, al-Daylami, and Abu Nasr al-Sijzi in al-Ibanah narrated from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not ask the People of the Book about anything, for they will not guide you, and they have gone astray. Either you will affirm something false, or you will deny something true. By Allah, if Musa were alive among you, it would not be lawful for him except to follow me."

'Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Do not ask the People of the Book," and he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Jabir, then said: "If you must ask them, then look at what agrees with the Book of Allah and take it, and what contradicts the Book of Allah and leave it."

(p-1121) **His saying:** ﴿The likeness of those who take other than Allah as protectors﴾ means those who make them allies and rely on them for their needs, apart from Allah, whether they are inanimate objects or animals, living or dead. ﴿Is like the spider that takes a house﴾. Indeed, its house does not benefit it at all, neither against heat, nor cold, nor rain. Likewise, what they have taken as a protector besides Allah does not benefit them in any way of benefit and does not avail them anything.

Al-Farra' said: This is a parable that Allah has coined for one who takes other gods besides Him, which do not benefit or harm him, just as the spider's house does not shield it from heat or cold.

He said: It is not good to stop at "al-'Ankabut" (the spider), because when the comparison is made to its house, which does not shield it from anything, the gods that neither benefit nor harm are compared to it. Al-Akhfash permitted pausing at "al-'Ankabut," but Ibn al-Anbari considered this an error, saying: "Because *ittakhadhat* (took) is a *silah* (relative clause) of *al-'Ankabut*, as if he had said: 'Like the spider that took a house.' So it is not good to stop at the *silah* without the *mawsul* (the relative pronoun/noun it modifies)." *Al-'Ankabut* applies to the singular and plural, masculine and feminine. Its plurals are *'anakib* and *'ankabutat*. It is a small insect that weaves a fine web. It is also said: *la-ha 'akanbat*, and from this is the poet's verse:

> As if there falls from its saliva
> A house of spider-webs upon its bridle.

﴿And indeed the weakest of houses is the house of the spider﴾: there is no house weaker than it among what insects take as a house, and nothing comes close to it in frailty and fragility, if they only knew that taking protectors besides Allah is like the spider taking a house. Or if they knew anything of knowledge, they would have known this.

﴿Indeed, Allah knows whatever they call upon besides Him of anything﴾: *ma* may be interrogative, negative, or relative, and *min* may be partitive or emphatic (*zā'idah li-l-ta'kīd*).

It was also said that this sentence is governed by an implied "say" (*idmar al-qawl*), meaning: "Say to the disbelievers: Indeed Allah knows whatever they call upon besides Him."

Abu 'Ali al-Farisi affirmed that it is interrogative. On the basis of a negative, it is as if it were said: "Indeed Allah knows that you do not call upon anything besides Him," meaning: what you call upon is not a thing. On the basis of a relative, it means: "Indeed Allah knows those whom you call upon besides Him." It is also permissible for *ma* to be a verbal noun (*maṣdariyyah*), and *min shay'* would then be an expression for the verbal noun.

ʿĀṣim, Abu ʿAmr, and Yaʿqub read *yad'ūna* with the third person (*bi-l-taḥtiyyah*). Abu ʿUbayd preferred this reading because the peoples were mentioned before this verse. The rest read it with the second person (*bi-l-fawqiyyah*), as addressed speech. ﴿And He is the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾: the Victorious, the Wise, who brings His actions to the utmost degree of perfection and precision.

﴿And these parables We coin for the people﴾: that is, this parable and others like it in the Qur'an, which We coin for people as a warning to them and to bring closer to their understanding what is far from it. ﴿And none understand them except the knowledgeable﴾, that is, none understand and comprehend the matter for which We coined them except those who know Allah, the firmly rooted in knowledge, who reflect and contemplate what is recited to them and what they witness.

﴿Allah created the heavens and the earth with truth﴾: that is, with justice and equity, taking into account in their creation the welfare of His servants.

It was also said: The meaning of "truth" is His speech and His power. The position of *bi-l-ḥaqq* is accusative as a circumstantial clause (*ḥāl*). ﴿Indeed in that is a sign for the believers﴾: that is, indeed there is a great proof and a manifest indication of His power and His singularity in divinity. He specified the believers because they are the ones who benefit from it.

﴿Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book﴾: that is, the Qur'an. In it is the command to recite the Qur'an, to be steadfast in reading it, reflecting on its verses and contemplating its meanings. ﴿And establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing﴾: that is, persist in establishing it and continue in performing it as you have been commanded. The clause ﴿indeed prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing﴾ is a reason for what precedes it. *Al-fahshā'* is what is ugly of deeds, and *al-munkar* is what is not recognized in the Sharia. That is, it prevents one from the disobedience of Allah and keeps one away from it. The meaning of its prohibiting this is that performing it is a cause for refraining. What is intended here is the obligatory prayers. ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾: that is, greater than everything, meaning more excellent than all acts of worship without remembrance.

Ibn ʿAṭiyyah said: In my view the meaning is: "And the remembrance of Allah is greater" absolutely, that is, it is what prohibits immorality and wrongdoing. So the part of it that occurs during prayer does this, and it also does what does not occur in prayer, because refraining only comes from one who remembers Allah and is mindful of Him.

It was also said: The remembrance of Allah is greater than prayer in forbidding immorality and wrongdoing, together with its constancy. Al-Farra' and Ibn Qutaybah said: What is meant by "remembrance" in the verse is glorification (*tasbīḥ*) and declaration of His oneness (*tahlīl*). One says: He is greater, and more worthy of forbidding immorality and wrongdoing.

It was also said: What is meant by "remembrance" here is prayer, that is, prayer is greater than the rest of the acts of obedience. He expressed it as "remembrance," as in His saying: ﴿So hasten to the remembrance of Allah﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 9], to indicate that the remembrance it contains is the principal basis for its superiority over the rest of the acts of obedience.

It was also said: The meaning is: And the remembrance of Allah toward you, with reward and praise from Him upon you, is greater than your remembrance of Him in your worship and your prayers. Ibn Jarir chose this view, and it is supported by the hadith: "Whoever remembers Me in himself, I remember him in Myself, and whoever remembers Me in an assembly, I remember him in an assembly better than them." ﴿And Allah knows what you do﴾: nothing of that is hidden from Him, so He will recompense you with good for good and with evil for evil.

﴿And do not argue with the People of the Book except in the best manner﴾: that is, except with the way that is best. This is by way of calling them to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and drawing their attention to His proofs and evidences, hoping they will respond by embracing Islam, not by way of harshness and roughness. ﴿Except those of them who have wronged﴾: that is, by going to excess in argument and not behaving courteously toward the Muslims. There is then no harm in being harsh with them and rough in arguing with them. Thus most exegetes explained the verse, that the People of the Book meant the Jews and the Christians.

It was also said: The meaning of the verse is: Do not argue with those among the People of the Book who believed in Muhammad, such as ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam and all others among them who believed, except in the best manner, meaning by agreeing with what they tell you of the reports of the People of the Book. According to this view, those "who have wronged" are those who remained upon their disbelief.

It was also said: This verse is abrogated (*mansūkhah*) by the verses of fighting (*āyāt al-qitāl*). Qatadah and Muqatil said so. Al-Nahhas said: Whoever says it is abrogated argues that the verse is Meccan, and at that time there was no obligatory fighting, nor demand for the poll-tax (*jizyah*), nor anything else of that kind.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid said: What is meant by "those of them who have wronged" are those who took up war against the Muslims, so arguing with them is by the sword until they embrace Islam or pay the poll-tax. ﴿And say: We believe in what has been revealed to us﴾ of the Qur'an, ﴿and what has been revealed to you (p-1122) of the Torah and the Gospel﴾, that is: we believe that both are sent down from Allah, and that they are a law that remains valid until the establishment of the Islamic law and the mission of Muhammad. This does not include what they have distorted and altered. ﴿Our God and your God is one﴾, having no partner, no equal, and no rival. ﴿And we are Muslims to Him﴾: that is, we, the community of Muhammad, obey Him exclusively. We did not say that ʿUzayr is the son of Allah, nor that the Messiah is the son of Allah, nor did we take our rabbis and monks as lords besides Allah. It is also possible that what is meant is: "and we are all submitting to Him." That this interpretation considers the submission of the Muslims more complete than the submission of the People of the Book, and their obedience more emphatic than theirs, does not weaken this meaning.

﴿Allah created the heavens and the earth with truth﴾: that is, with justice and equity, taking into account in their creation the welfare of His servants.

It was also said: The meaning of "truth" is His speech and His power. The position of *bi-l-ḥaqq* is accusative as a circumstantial clause (*ḥāl*). ﴿Indeed in that is a sign for the believers﴾: that is, indeed there is a great proof and a manifest indication of His power and His singularity in divinity. He specified the believers because they are the ones who benefit from it.

﴿Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book﴾: that is, the Qur'an. In it is the command to recite the Qur'an, to be steadfast in reading it, reflecting on its verses and contemplating its meanings. ﴿And establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing﴾: that is, persist in establishing it and continue in performing it as you have been commanded. The clause ﴿indeed prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing﴾ is a reason for what precedes it. *Al-fahshā'* is what is ugly of deeds, and *al-munkar* is what is not recognized in the Sharia. That is, it prevents one from the disobedience of Allah and keeps one away from it. The meaning of its prohibiting this is that performing it is a cause for refraining. What is intended here is the obligatory prayers. ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾: that is, greater than everything, meaning more excellent than all acts of worship without remembrance.

Ibn ʿAṭiyyah said: In my view the meaning is: "And the remembrance of Allah is greater" absolutely, that is, it is what prohibits immorality and wrongdoing. So the part of it that occurs during prayer does this, and it also does what does not occur in prayer, because refraining only comes from one who remembers Allah and is mindful of Him.

It was also said: The remembrance of Allah is greater than prayer in forbidding immorality and wrongdoing, together with its constancy. Al-Farra' and Ibn Qutaybah said: What is meant by "remembrance" in the verse is glorification (*tasbīḥ*) and declaration of His oneness (*tahlīl*). One says: He is greater, and more worthy of forbidding immorality and wrongdoing.

It was also said: What is meant by "remembrance" here is prayer, that is, prayer is greater than the rest of the acts of obedience. He expressed it as "remembrance," as in His saying: ﴿So hasten to the remembrance of Allah﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 9], to indicate that the remembrance it contains is the principal basis for its superiority over the rest of the acts of obedience.

It was also said: The meaning is: And the remembrance of Allah toward you, with reward and praise from Him upon you, is greater than your remembrance of Him in your worship and your prayers. Ibn Jarir chose this view, and it is supported by the hadith: "Whoever remembers Me in himself, I remember him in Myself, and whoever remembers Me in an assembly, I remember him in an assembly better than them." ﴿And Allah knows what you do﴾: nothing of that is hidden from Him, so He will recompense you with good for good and with evil for evil.

﴿And do not argue with the People of the Book except in the best manner﴾: that is, except with the way that is best. This is by way of calling them to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and drawing their attention to His proofs and evidences, hoping they will respond by embracing Islam, not by way of harshness and roughness. ﴿Except those of them who have wronged﴾: that is, by going to excess in argument and not behaving courteously toward the Muslims. There is then no harm in being harsh with them and rough in arguing with them. Thus most exegetes explained the verse, that the People of the Book meant the Jews and the Christians.

It was also said: The meaning of the verse is: Do not argue with those among the People of the Book who believed in Muhammad, such as ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam and all others among them who believed, except in the best manner, meaning by agreeing with what they tell you of the reports of the People of the Book. According to this view, those "who have wronged" are those who remained upon their disbelief.

It was also said: This verse is abrogated (*mansūkhah*) by the verses of fighting (*āyāt al-qitāl*). Qatadah and Muqatil said so. Al-Nahhas said: Whoever says it is abrogated argues that the verse is Meccan, and at that time there was no obligatory fighting, nor demand for the poll-tax (*jizyah*), nor anything else of that kind.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid said: What is meant by "those of them who have wronged" are those who took up war against the Muslims, so arguing with them is by the sword until they embrace Islam or pay the poll-tax. ﴿And say: We believe in what has been revealed to us﴾ of the Qur'an, ﴿and what has been revealed to you (p-1122) of the Torah and the Gospel﴾, that is: we believe that both are sent down from Allah, and that they are a law that remains valid until the establishment of the Islamic law and the mission of Muhammad. This does not include what they have distorted and altered. ﴿Our God and your God is one﴾, having no partner, no equal, and no rival. ﴿And we are Muslims to Him﴾: that is, we, the community of Muhammad, obey Him exclusively. We did not say that ʿUzayr is the son of Allah, nor that the Messiah is the son of Allah, nor did we take our rabbis and monks as lords besides Allah. It is also possible that what is meant is: "and we are all submitting to Him." That this interpretation considers the submission of the Muslims more complete than the submission of the People of the Book, and their obedience more emphatic than theirs, does not weaken this meaning.

Ibn Jarir reported from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿The likeness of those who take other than Allah as protectors﴾, the verse, that he said: That is a parable Allah coined for one who worships other than Him: his likeness is like the likeness of the spider's house.

Abu Dawud reported in his *Marasil* from Yazid ibn Marthad, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The spider is a devil whom Allah transformed. Whoever finds it, let him kill it."

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Mazid ibn Maysarah, who said: The spider is a devil.

Al-Khatib reported from ʿAli, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I and Abu Bakr entered the cave, and the spiders gathered and wove at the entrance, so do not kill them."

Al-Qurtubi related in his *Tafsir* from ʿAli also, that he said: Clean your houses of spider-webs, for leaving it in the house brings poverty.

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from ʿAta' al-Khurasani, who said: The spider wove twice: once over Dawud, and a second time over the Prophet (ﷺ).

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing﴾, that he said: In prayer there is a restraint and a deterrent from sins.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh reported from ʿImran ibn Husayn, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about the saying of Allah: ﴿Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing﴾, and he said: "Whoever his prayer does not forbid immorality and wrongdoing, there is no prayer for him."

Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh reported from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever his prayer does not forbid immorality and wrongdoing, he increases in nothing through it from Allah except distance."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Shuʿab* reported from al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever his prayer does not forbid immorality and wrongdoing, there is no prayer for him." In another wording: "He does not increase through it from Allah except distance."

Al-Khatib reported from Ibn ʿUmar, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), something similar. ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Mardawayh reported from Ibn Masʿud, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), something similar. Al-Suyuti said: Its chain is weak.

Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ahmad in *al-Zuhd*, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Tabarani in *al-Shuʿab* reported something similar from him as a statement of his own (*mawquf*).

Ibn Kathir said in his *Tafsir*: The most authentic of all of this are the statements (*mawqufat*) from Ibn Masʿud, Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Aʿmash, and others.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾, that he said: The remembrance of Allah of His servants, when they remember Him, is greater than their remembrance of Him.

Al-Firyabi, Sa'd ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Shuʿab* reported from ʿAbd Allah ibn Rabiʿah, who said: Ibn ʿAbbas asked me about the saying of Allah: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾. I said: The remembrance of Allah is by glorification, declaration of His oneness, and magnification. He said: The remembrance of Allah of you is greater than your remembrance of Him. Then he said: "Remember Me, and I will remember you."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad in *Zawa'id al-Zuhd*, and Ibn Jarir reported from Ibn Masʿud regarding ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾, that he said: The remembrance of Allah of the servant is greater than the remembrance of the servant of Allah.

Ibn al-Sunni, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Daylami reported something similar from Ibn ʿUmar.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding the verse, that he said: It has two aspects: the remembrance of Allah is greater than anything else. In another wording: the remembrance of Allah at what He has forbidden, and the remembrance of Allah of you is greater than your remembrance of Him.

Ahmad in *al-Zuhd* and Ibn al-Mundhir reported from Muʿadh ibn Jabal, who said: No human has performed any deed that is more saving for him from the punishment of Allah than the remembrance of Allah. They said: Not even jihad in the path of Allah? He said: Not even if he strikes with his sword until it breaks, because Allah says in His Mighty Book: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 29, verse 41–46 (part 2 of 2):

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim in al-Kuna, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated from 'Anbasah, who said: I said to Ibn 'Abbas, "Which deed is the best?" He said: "The remembrance of Allah."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him regarding His saying: ﴿And do not argue with the People of the Book except in a way that is best﴾ that he said: "[It is] 'There is no god but Allah.'"

al-Bukhari, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "The People of the Book used to recite the Torah in Hebrew and explain it to the People of Islam in Arabic. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Do not believe the People of the Book, nor disbelieve them, but say: We believe in what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to you, and our God and your God is One, and to Him we are submitting.'"

al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab, al-Daylami, and Abu Nasr al-Sijzi in al-Ibanah narrated from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not ask the People of the Book about anything, for they will not guide you, and they have gone astray. Either you will affirm something false, or you will deny something true. By Allah, if Musa were alive among you, it would not be lawful for him except to follow me."

'Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Do not ask the People of the Book," and he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Jabir, then said: "If you must ask them, then look at what agrees with the Book of Allah and take it, and what contradicts the Book of Allah and leave it."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 29, verses 47–55:

(p-1123) His saying: ﴿And thus We have sent down to you the Book﴾. This is an address to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the reference (al-ishara) is to the source (masdar) of the verb, as we have explained in many places.

That is: Like that wondrous sending down, We have sent down to you the Book, which is the Qur'an. It was said: the meaning is, just as We sent down the Book upon them, We have sent down the Qur'an upon you. ﴿Those to whom We have given the Book believe in it﴾, meaning the believers among the People of the Book, such as ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam. He singled them out by giving them the Book because they are the ones who act upon it, whereas the others are as though they were not given it, due to their not acting upon what is in it and their denial of the attributes of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mentioned therein. ﴿And among these there are those who believe in it﴾: the reference is to the people of Makkah, and the meaning is that among them are those who have embraced Islam and believe in it, i.e., in the Qur'an. It was said: the reference is to all the Arabs. ﴿And none deny Our signs except the disbelievers﴾, i.e., the signs of the Qur'an, except the disbelievers who are obstinate in their disbelief, from among the polytheists and the People of the Book.

﴿And you did not recite any Book before it﴾: the pronoun in qablihi (before it) refers to the Qur'an, because it is what is meant by His saying "We have sent down to you the Book." That is: O Muhammad, you did not used to read any book before the Qur'an, nor were you able to do so, because you are an unlettered man who neither reads nor writes. ﴿Nor did you write it with your right hand﴾, i.e., nor did you write it, because you were not able to write.

Mujahid said: The People of the Book would find in their books that Muhammad (ﷺ) would neither write nor read, so this verse was revealed.

Al-Nahhas said: This is evidence of his prophethood, because he neither wrote nor mixed with the People of the Book, and there were no People of the Book in Makkah, yet he brought them reports of the prophets and the nations. ﴿Otherwise the falsifiers would have had doubt﴾: that is, had you been one who could read and write, they would have said, "Perhaps he found what he recites to us from the earlier books of Allah, or from the written books concerning the reports of the nations." But since you were unlettered, neither reading nor writing, there was no place for suspicion and no ground for doubt at all. Rather, the denial of those who denied and the disbelief of those who disbelieved is mere obstinacy and denial without any basis. He called them "falsifiers" (mubtiluna) because their doubt, on the assumption that he (ﷺ) could read and write, would be an injustice on their part, given the clear evidence of his integrity and the manifest nature of his miracles.

﴿Rather, it is clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge﴾: meaning the Qur'an, and the believers who memorized the Qur'an during his lifetime (ﷺ) and memorized it after him are meant by "those given knowledge." Qatadah and Muqatil said: the pronoun refers to the Prophet (ﷺ), i.e., rather Muhammad is clear signs, meaning possessor of signs.

Ibn Mas'ud recited "Rather, they are clear signs." Al-Farra' said the meaning of this reading is: rather, the signs of the Qur'an are clear signs.

Ibn Jarir preferred what Qatadah and Muqatil said, and he cited as evidence for their view the reading of Ibn al-Sumaifa' "Rather, this is clear signs." But there is no proof in this reading for that, because the demonstrative may refer to the Qur'an just as it may refer to the Prophet (ﷺ). Indeed, its reference to the Qur'an is more apparent, since it does not need interpretation or supposition. ﴿And none deny Our signs except the wrongdoers﴾, i.e., those who exceed the limit in wrongdoing.

﴿And they say: Why has not a sign been sent down to him from his Lord?﴾ That is, the polytheists said this statement, and the meaning is: Why were not signs like the signs of the prophets sent down to him, such as the signs of Moses, the she-camel of Salih, and the raising of the dead by the Messiah? Then Allah, exalted is He, commanded him to respond to them, so He said: ﴿Say: Signs are only with Allah﴾, He sends them down upon whomever He wills of His servants, and no one has power over that. "I am only a clear warner," warning you as I was commanded and explaining to you as is fitting; I have no power beyond that.

Ibn Kathir, Abu Bakr, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "lawla unzila ʿalayhi ayah" in the singular.

The rest read it in the plural. Abu ʿUbaid preferred this reading because of His saying "Say: Signs are only with Allah."

﴿Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book being recited to them?﴾ This sentence is a new clause (mustaʾnafah) responding to their demand and showing its falsehood. That is: Is it not sufficient for the polytheists, among the signs they proposed, this Book, the inimitable one, with which you have challenged them to produce its like or a single surah of it, and they were unable? Even if you had brought them the signs of Moses and the signs of other prophets, they would not have believed, just as they did not believe in the Qur'an, which is recited to them in every time and place. Indeed, in that is a reference to the Book described as such: it is a great mercy in this world and the next, and a reminder (dhikra) in this world by which they remember and which guides them to the truth, for a people who believe, i.e., a people who affirm what you have brought from Allah, for they are the ones who benefit from it.

﴿Say: Allah suffices as a witness between me and you﴾, i.e., say to the deniers: Allah suffices as a witness to what has occurred between me and you. He knows what is in the heavens and the earth; nothing of that is hidden from Him, and among that is what has passed between you and His Messenger. ﴿And those who believe in falsehood and disbelieve in Allah—those are the losers﴾, i.e., they believed in what they worship besides Allah and disbelieved in the Truth, which is Allah, exalted is He. Those are the ones who combine the loss of this world and the next.

﴿And they ask you to hasten the punishment﴾, mockingly and in denial, as they said: ﴿Then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment﴾ [al-Anfal: 32]. ﴿Had there not been a specified term﴾: Allah has appointed a term for their punishment and fixed it, and it is the Resurrection. Al-Dahhak said: the term is the span of their lives, because when they die they proceed to punishment; "the punishment would have come upon them," i.e., had it not been for that appointed term, the punishment they deserve for their sins would have come upon them.

It was said: the specified term refers to the first blast (al-nafkha al-ula). It was also said: the time Allah decreed for their punishment in this world by killing and capture on the day of Badr.

The summary is that every punishment has a term which it cannot precede or lag behind, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿For every news there is a settled time﴾ [al-An'am: 67]. The clause "and it will come upon them suddenly" is a new clause explaining the coming of the punishment mentioned before it. The meaning of baghtatan (suddenly) is unexpectedly, and the clause "while they do not perceive" is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal), i.e., while they are unaware of its coming. Then He, exalted is He, mentioned that the place of their punishment is the Fire, so He said: ﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment, and indeed Hell will surround the disbelievers﴾. That is: they ask you to hasten their punishment, while the place of punishment already encompasses them; that is, it will surround them soon, for what is coming is near. The "disbelievers" here refers to the category, so these askers enter into it primarily. His saying "They ask you to hasten the punishment" (p-1124) is a report about them, and His saying a second time "They ask you to hasten the punishment" is an expression of wonder at them. It was said: the repetition is for emphasis.

Then He, exalted is He, mentioned the manner in which the punishment will encompass them, saying: ﴿On the Day the punishment will cover them from above them and from beneath their feet﴾, i.e., from all their directions. When the punishment overtakes them in this manner, Hell has indeed encompassed them. ﴿And He will say: Taste what you used to do﴾. The speaker is Allah, exalted is He, or some of His angels by His command, i.e., taste the recompense for what you used to do of disbelief and sins.

Ahl al-Madinah and the Kufans read "naqulu" with the nun. The rest read it with the yaʾ, and Abu ʿUbaid preferred the latter reading because of His saying "Say: Allah suffices." Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abi ʿAblah read "wa-yuqalu dhuqu."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Isma'ili in his Mu'jam have reported from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿And you did not recite any Book before it, nor did you write it with your right hand﴾, that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not read or write; he was unlettered. And regarding His saying: ﴿Rather, it is clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge﴾, he said: Allah had sent down the matter of Muhammad in the Torah and the Gospel to the people of knowledge and taught it to them, and made it a sign for them, saying to them: The sign of his prophethood is that he will emerge when he emerges, not knowing a book nor writing it with his right hand. These are the clear signs of which Allah, exalted is He, spoke.

Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan reported from Ibn Mas'ud regarding His saying: ﴿And you did not recite any Book before it﴾ and the rest of the verse, that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not read or write.

Al-Firyabi, al-Darimi, and Abu Dawud in his Marasil, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Yahya ibn Ja'dah who said: "Some Muslims came with books they had written, containing some of what they had heard from the Jews. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: It is enough folly or misguidance for a people that they turn away from what their Prophet brought them to what others have brought to others. So the verse 'Is it not sufficient for them' was revealed."

Al-Isma'ili in his Mu'jam and Ibn Mardawayh reported it through the chain of Yahya ibn Ja'dah from Abu Hurayrah, with the same meaning.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq in his Musannaf and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shuʿab reported from al-Zuhri that "Hafsah came to the Prophet (ﷺ) with a book of the story of Yusuf on a shoulder-blade, and she began reading it while the Prophet's face changed color. He said: By Him in whose hand is my soul, if Yusuf came to you and I was your prophet, and you followed him and left me, you would have gone astray."

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Ibn Sa'd, Ibn al-Dhurays, al-Hakim in al-Kuna, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shuʿab reported from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Harith al-Ansari who said: "ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab entered upon the Prophet (ﷺ) with a book containing passages from the Torah and said: I have acquired this with a man from the People of the Book; I will present it to you. The face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) changed severely, the like of which I had never seen. ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Harith said to ʿUmar: Do you not see the face of the Messenger of Allah? ʿUmar said: We are pleased with Allah as Lord, Islam as religion, and Muhammad as prophet. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was relieved and said: If Moses came down and you followed him and left me, you would have gone astray. I am your portion of the prophets, and you are my portion of the nations."

ʿAbd al-Razzaq and al-Bayhaqi reported something similar through the chain of Abu Qilabah from ʿUmar.

Al-Bayhaqi reported and authenticated it from ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab who said: "I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about learning the Torah, and he said: Do not learn it, but believe in it, and learn what has been sent down to you and believe in it."

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿And indeed Hell will surround the disbelievers﴾ that he said: Jahannam is this green sea, in which the stars scatter and the sun and moon are, and then it is kindled and becomes Jahannam. In this there is severe strangeness, for the many authentic hadiths affirm that Jahannam exists, created, with the attributes in which the Book and the Sunnah have described it.

Mujahid said: The People of the Book would find in their books that Muhammad (ﷺ) would neither write nor read, so this verse was revealed.

Ibn Jarir preferred what Qatadah and Muqatil said, and he cited as evidence for their view the reading of Ibn al-Sumaifa' "Rather, this is clear signs." Then Allah, exalted is He, commanded him to respond to them, so He said: ﴿Say: Signs are only with Allah﴾, He sends them down upon whomever He wills of His servants, and no one has power over that. Mujahid said: The People of the Book would find in their books that Muhammad (ﷺ) would neither write nor read, so this verse was revealed.

Qatadah and Muqatil said: the pronoun refers to the Prophet (ﷺ), i.e., rather Muhammad is clear signs, meaning possessor of signs.

Ibn Mas'ud recited "Rather, they are clear signs." Al-Farra' said the meaning of this reading is: rather, the signs of the Qur'an are clear signs.

Ibn Jarir preferred what Qatadah and Muqatil said, and he cited as evidence for their view the reading of Ibn al-Sumaifa' "Rather, this is clear signs." Ibn Kathir, Abu Bakr, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "lawla unzila ʿalayhi ayah" in the singular.

The rest read it in the plural. Abu ʿUbaid preferred this reading because of His saying "Say: Signs are only with Allah."

That is: O Muhammad, you did not used to read any book before the Qur'an, nor were you able to do so, because you are an unlettered man who neither reads nor writes. ﴿Nor did you write it with your right hand﴾, i.e., nor did you write it, because you were not able to write.

Mujahid said: The People of the Book would find in their books that Muhammad (ﷺ) would neither write nor read, so this verse was revealed.

Al-Nahhas said: This is evidence of his prophethood, because he neither wrote nor mixed with the People of the Book, and there were no People of the Book in Makkah, yet he brought them reports of the prophets and the nations. ﴿Otherwise the falsifiers would have had doubt﴾: that is, had you been one who could read and write, they would have said, "Perhaps he found what he recites to us from the earlier books of Allah, or from the written books concerning the reports of the nations." But since you were unlettered, neither reading nor writing, there was no place for suspicion and no ground for doubt at all. Rather, the denial of those who denied and the disbelief of those who disbelieved is mere obstinacy and denial without any basis. He called them "falsifiers" (mubtiluna) because their doubt, on the assumption that he (ﷺ) could read and write, would be an injustice on their part, given the clear evidence of his integrity and the manifest nature of his miracles.

﴿Rather, it is clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge﴾: meaning the Qur'an, and the believers who memorized the Qur'an during his lifetime (ﷺ) and memorized it after him are meant by "those given knowledge." Qatadah and Muqatil said: the pronoun refers to the Prophet (ﷺ), i.e., rather Muhammad is clear signs, meaning possessor of signs.

Ibn Mas'ud recited "Rather, they are clear signs." Al-Farra' said the meaning of this reading is: rather, the signs of the Qur'an are clear signs.

Ibn Jarir preferred what Qatadah and Muqatil said, and he cited as evidence for their view the reading of Ibn al-Sumaifa' "Rather, this is clear signs." But there is no proof in this reading for that, because the demonstrative may refer to the Qur'an just as it may refer to the Prophet (ﷺ). Indeed, its reference to the Qur'an is more apparent, since it does not need interpretation or supposition. ﴿And none deny Our signs except the wrongdoers﴾, i.e., those who exceed the limit in wrongdoing.

﴿And they say: Why has not a sign been sent down to him from his Lord?﴾ That is, the polytheists said this statement, and the meaning is: Why were not signs like the signs of the prophets sent down to him, such as the signs of Moses, the she-camel of Salih, and the raising of the dead by the Messiah? Then Allah, exalted is He, commanded him to respond to them, so He said: ﴿Say: Signs are only with Allah﴾, He sends them down upon whomever He wills of His servants, and no one has power over that. "I am only a clear warner," warning you as I was commanded and explaining to you as is fitting; I have no power beyond that.

Ibn Kathir, Abu Bakr, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "lawla unzila ʿalayhi ayah" in the singular.

The rest read it in the plural. Abu ʿUbaid preferred this reading because of His saying "Say: Signs are only with Allah."

﴿Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book being recited to them?﴾ This sentence is a new clause (mustaʾnafah) responding to their demand and showing its falsehood. That is: Is it not sufficient for the polytheists, among the signs they proposed, this Book, the inimitable one, with which you have challenged them to produce its like or a single surah of it, and they were unable? Even if you had brought them the signs of Moses and the signs of other prophets, they would not have believed, just as they did not believe in the Qur'an, which is recited to them in every time and place. Indeed, in that is a reference to the Book described as such: it is a great mercy in this world and the next, and a reminder (dhikra) in this world by which they remember and which guides them to the truth, for a people who believe, i.e., a people who affirm what you have brought from Allah, for they are the ones who benefit from it.

﴿Say: Allah suffices as a witness between me and you﴾, i.e., say to the deniers: Allah suffices as a witness to what has occurred between me and you. He knows what is in the heavens and the earth; nothing of that is hidden from Him, and among that is what has passed between you and His Messenger. ﴿And those who believe in falsehood and disbelieve in Allah—those are the losers﴾, i.e., they believed in what they worship besides Allah and disbelieved in the Truth, which is Allah, exalted is He. Those are the ones who combine the loss of this world and the next.

﴿And they ask you to hasten the punishment﴾, mockingly and in denial, as they said: ﴿Then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment﴾ [al-Anfal: 32]. ﴿Had there not been a specified term﴾: Allah has appointed a term for their punishment and fixed it, and it is the Resurrection. Al-Dahhak said: the term is the span of their lives, because when they die they proceed to punishment; "the punishment would have come upon them," i.e., had it not been for that appointed term, the punishment they deserve for their sins would have come upon them.

It was said: the specified term refers to the first blast (al-nafkha al-ula). It was also said: the time Allah decreed for their punishment in this world by killing and capture on the day of Badr.

The summary is that every punishment has a term which it cannot precede or lag behind, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿For every news there is a settled time﴾ [al-An'am: 67]. The clause "and it will come upon them suddenly" is a new clause explaining the coming of the punishment mentioned before it. The meaning of baghtatan (suddenly) is unexpectedly, and the clause "while they do not perceive" is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal), i.e., while they are unaware of its coming. Then He, exalted is He, mentioned that the place of their punishment is the Fire, so He said: ﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment, and indeed Hell will surround the disbelievers﴾. That is: they ask you to hasten their punishment, while the place of punishment already encompasses them; that is, it will surround them soon, for what is coming is near. The "disbelievers" here refers to the category, so these askers enter into it primarily. His saying "They ask you to hasten the punishment" (p-1124) is a report about them, and His saying a second time "They ask you to hasten the punishment" is an expression of wonder at them. It was said: the repetition is for emphasis.

Then He, exalted is He, mentioned the manner in which the punishment will encompass them, saying: ﴿On the Day the punishment will cover them from above them and from beneath their feet﴾, i.e., from all their directions. When the punishment overtakes them in this manner, Hell has indeed encompassed them. ﴿And He will say: Taste what you used to do﴾. The speaker is Allah, exalted is He, or some of His angels by His command, i.e., taste the recompense for what you used to do of disbelief and sins.

Ahl al-Madinah and the Kufans read "naqulu" with the nun. The rest read it with the yaʾ, and Abu ʿUbaid preferred the latter reading because of His saying "Say: Allah suffices." Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abi ʿAblah read "wa-yuqalu dhuqu."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Isma'ili in his Mu'jam have reported from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿And you did not recite any Book before it, nor did you write it with your right hand﴾, that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not read or write; he was unlettered. And regarding His saying: ﴿Rather, it is clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge﴾, he said: Allah had sent down the matter of Muhammad in the Torah and the Gospel to the people of knowledge and taught it to them, and made it a sign for them, saying to them: The sign of his prophethood is that he will emerge when he emerges, not knowing a book nor writing it with his right hand. These are the clear signs of which Allah, exalted is He, spoke.

Al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan reported from Ibn Mas'ud regarding His saying: ﴿And you did not recite any Book before it﴾ and the rest of the verse, that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not read or write.

Al-Firyabi, al-Darimi, and Abu Dawud in his Marasil, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Yahya ibn Ja'dah who said: "Some Muslims came with books they had written, containing some of what they had heard from the Jews. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: It is enough folly or misguidance for a people that they turn away from what their Prophet brought them to what others have brought to others. So the verse 'Is it not sufficient for them' was revealed."

Al-Isma'ili in his Mu'jam and Ibn Mardawayh reported it through the chain of Yahya ibn Ja'dah from Abu Hurayrah, with the same meaning.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq in his Musannaf and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shuʿab reported from al-Zuhri that "Hafsah came to the Prophet (ﷺ) with a book of the story of Yusuf on a shoulder-blade, and she began reading it while the Prophet's face changed color. He said: By Him in whose hand is my soul, if Yusuf came to you and I was your prophet, and you followed him and left me, you would have gone astray."

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Ibn Sa'd, Ibn al-Dhurays, al-Hakim in al-Kuna, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shuʿab reported from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Harith al-Ansari who said: "ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab entered upon the Prophet (ﷺ) with a book containing passages from the Torah and said: I have acquired this with a man from the People of the Book; I will present it to you. The face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) changed severely, the like of which I had never seen. ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Harith said to ʿUmar: Do you not see the face of the Messenger of Allah? ʿUmar said: We are pleased with Allah as Lord, Islam as religion, and Muhammad as prophet. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was relieved and said: If Moses came down and you followed him and left me, you would have gone astray. I am your portion of the prophets, and you are my portion of the nations."

ʿAbd al-Razzaq and al-Bayhaqi reported something similar through the chain of Abu Qilabah from ʿUmar.

Al-Bayhaqi reported and authenticated it from ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab who said: "I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about learning the Torah, and he said: Do not learn it, but believe in it, and learn what has been sent down to you and believe in it."

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿And indeed Hell will surround the disbelievers﴾ that he said: Jahannam is this green sea, in which the stars scatter and the sun and moon are, and then it is kindled and becomes Jahannam. In this there is severe strangeness, for the many authentic hadiths affirm that Jahannam exists, created, with the attributes in which the Book and the Sunnah have described it.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 29, verses 56–69 (part 1 of 2):

When He, glory be to Him, mentioned the condition of the disbelievers among the People of the Book and the polytheists, grouped them together in the warning, and made them among the people of the Fire, their obstinacy intensified, their corruption increased, and they strove to harm the Muslims in every way. So Allah, glory be to Him, said: ﴿O My servants who have believed﴾. He attributed them to Himself after addressing them, as an honour and a mark of dignity. The phrase ﴿who have believed﴾ is a descriptive qualifier, either explanatory or distinguishing. ﴿Indeed, My earth is spacious﴾: if you are in straitened circumstances in Makkah due to displaying faith and due to the plotting of the disbelievers, then leave it, so that My worship alone may be made easy for you and made smooth for you.

103 Al-Zajjaj said: They were commanded to emigrate from the place where it is not possible for them to worship Allah. Likewise, whoever is in a land where sins are committed and cannot change that is obliged to emigrate to where he can prepare himself to worship Allah with the worship due to Him.

Mutarrif ibn al-Shikhkhir said: The meaning is: indeed My mercy is vast and My provision for you is ample, so seek it in the earth.

It was also said: The meaning is: indeed My earth, which is the earth of Paradise, is spacious, so worship Me and I will make you inherit it.

The accusative of ﴿iyya-ya﴾ (Me) is by a hidden verb, meaning: so worship Me.

Then He, glory be to Him, made them fear death in order to ease for them the matter of emigration, and said: ﴿Every soul shall taste death; then to Us you will be returned﴾. That is: every soul among souls will certainly experience the bitterness of death, so leaving homelands and parting from brothers and close friends should not be difficult for you. Then the return is to Allah by death and resurrection, not to anyone else. So every living being is on a journey to the abode of permanence, however long he remains in this abode.

﴿And those who have believed and done righteous deeds – We will surely settle them in lofty chambers of Paradise﴾. In this is encouragement to emigration, and that the reward of one who emigrates is to be in the chambers of Paradise. The meaning of ﴿lanubawwi'annahum﴾ (We will surely settle them) is: We will surely cause them to descend into the chambers of Paradise, which are its upper parts. The accusative of ﴿ghurafan﴾ (chambers) is either as a second object, by implying the meaning of "cause to descend" in ﴿nubawwi'annahum﴾, or as an adverb of place without implication, since ﴿nubawwi'annahum﴾ is only transitive to one object; or it is accusative by removal of the preposition, as a broadening: "in the chambers of Paradise". It is derived from ﴿mabā'a﴾, which means causing to descend.

Abu 'Amr, Ya'qub, al-Jahdari, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Ibn Muhaysin, al-A'mash, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read ﴿Ya ibadi﴾ with the ya' sukun, while the rest read it with fatha.

Ibn 'Amir read ﴿inna ardi﴾ with fatha on the ya', while the rest read it with sukun.

Al-Sulami and Abu Bakr on the authority of 'Asim read ﴿yarji'un﴾ with the ya' (third person), while the rest read it with the ta' (second person).

Ibn Mas'ud, al-A'mash, Yahya ibn Wthhab, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read ﴿lanathwiyannahum﴾ with the thā' (ث) in place of the bā' (ب), while the rest read it with bā'. The meaning of ﴿lanathwiyannahum﴾ with thā' is: We will surely give them chambers in which they will dwell, from ﴿thawā﴾, which is staying.

Al-Zajjaj said: It is said: "thawā al-rajulu" when he stayed, and "athwaytuhu" when you caused him to descend to a dwelling in which he stays.

Al-Akhfash said: I do not like this reading, because you do not say "athwaytuhu al-dār" but rather "fī al-dār," and there is no preposition in the verse on the second object. Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said: It is according to the intention of the preposition, then it was omitted, as you say "amartuka al-khayr," meaning "bi al-khayr."

Then He, glory be to Him, described those chambers, saying: ﴿Beneath them rivers flow﴾, that is: from beneath the chambers; ﴿abiding therein﴾, that is: in the chambers, they will never die forever, or in Paradise; the first is preferable. ﴿How excellent is the reward of the workers﴾: the object of praise is omitted, meaning: how excellent is the reward of the workers is their reward. The meaning is: those who work at righteous deeds.

Then He described these workers, saying: Those who were patient in the hardships of obligation and in the harm inflicted on them by the polytheists, and it is permissible for it to be accusative as a praise. ﴿And upon their Lord they rely﴾, that is: they entrust their affairs to Him in every undertaking and every withdrawal.

Then He, glory be to Him, mentioned what helps in patience and reliance, which is contemplating the state of animals, saying: ﴿And how many a creature there is that does not carry its provision; Allah provides for it and for you﴾. The discussion of ﴿ka'ayyin﴾ has already passed, and that its origin is ay, the particle of comparison (kāf) entered upon it and it came to carry the meaning of "kam" (how many), as Khalil and Sibawayh stated explicitly. Its estimate according to both of them is "like a great quantity of number, of creatures."

It was also said: the meaning is: "and how many a creature."

The meaning of ﴿does not carry its provision﴾ is: it is not able to carry its provision due to its weakness, and it does not store it. Rather, Allah provides for it from His bounty and provides for you. So how would they not rely upon Allah, with their strength and their capacity over the means of livelihood, just as it relies upon Allah despite its weakness and incapacity?

Al-Hasan said: It eats in its time; it stores nothing.

Mujahid said: It means birds and beasts, which eat with their mouths and carry nothing. And He is the All-Hearing who hears every thing heard, the All-Knowing of every thing known.

Then, glory be to Him, He mentioned the condition of the polytheists of Makkah and others, and the listener marvels at their acknowledging that He is their Creator and Provider, yet they do not affirm His oneness and abandon the worship of others. So He said: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon?" they would surely say, "Allah."﴾ That is: He created them; they cannot deny that, nor are they able to reject it. ﴿So how are they turned away?﴾ That is: how are they diverted from acknowledging His singularity in divinity, and that He alone has no partner? The interrogative is for denial and remoteness.

When the polytheists said to some of the believers: "If you were upon the truth, you would not be poor," He, glory be to Him, repelled that with His saying: ﴿Allah expands provision for whomever He wills of His servants and restricts it for him.﴾ That is: expanding provision and restricting it is from Allah, the Expander and the Restrainer; He expands it for whomever He wills and narrows it upon whomever He wills, according to what His wisdom requires and what befits the condition of His servants of restriction and expansion. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed Allah is Knowing of all things﴾, He knows what is good for His servants and what is corrupt for them.

﴿And if you asked them, "Who sent down water from the sky and gave life thereby to the earth after its death?" they would surely say, "Allah."﴾ That is: He sent it down and Allah gave life to the earth by it; they acknowledge that, finding no way to deny it.

Then, when they acknowledged this acknowledgment in these verses, which necessitates the falsity of what they are upon of polytheism and not singling out Allah, glory be to Him, in worship, He commanded His Messenger, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, to praise Allah for their acknowledgment and non-denial, despite their obstinacy and their rigidity in rejecting everything the Messenger of Allah brought of monotheism. So He said: ﴿Say, "Praise is to Allah." But most of them do not reason.﴾ That is: I praise Allah for making the truth with you and for manifesting your proof against them. Then He condemned them, saying: "But most of them do not reason," meaning the things that sensible people reason about.

Therefore they do not act upon what they have acknowledged, which requires the falsity of what they are upon, according to every sensible person.

Then, glory be to Him, He pointed to the belittling of this world and that it is of the nature of play and amusement, and that the true abode is the abode of the Hereafter. So He said: ﴿And this worldly life is nothing but amusement and play﴾, of the kind with which children amuse themselves and play. ﴿And indeed, the Hereafter is the home of life, if they only knew.﴾

Ibn Qutaybah and Abu 'Ubaydah said: "al-Hayawan" is "al-Hayah" (life).

Al-Wahidi said: This is the view of all the exegetes; they held that the meaning of "al-hayawan" here is life, and that it is a verbal noun equivalent to "al-hayah," like "al-nazawan" and "al-ghalayan," so the estimate is: "and indeed the Hereafter (p-1126) is the abode of life," or "possessing life," that is: the abode of enduring life that does not cease, which is not troubled by death, sickness, worry, or grief. Had they known anything of knowledge, they would not have preferred over it the perishable, troubled abode.

Then, glory be to Him, made clear that the thing preventing them from faith is nothing but the mere influence of life. So He said: ﴿And when they board ships, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion.﴾ That is: when their hope of life is cut off and they fear drowning, they return to the natural disposition, so they call upon Allah alone, appearing as those sincere to Him in religion through the sincerity of their intentions, and abandoning at that time the calling upon idols, knowing that none other than Allah – glory be to Him – can remove this great hardship that has descended upon them. ﴿But when He delivers them to the land, at once they associate others with Him.﴾ That is: they suddenly returned to polytheism and called upon other than Allah, glory be to Him.

Riding (rukūb) means being elevated, and it is transitive by itself; it was made transitive by the word "fī" only to indicate that the thing ridden is in itself of the category of places.

The lām in ﴿liyakfurū bi-mā ātaynāhum﴾ and in His saying "wa-liyatamatta'ū" is for causation, that is: they associate others with Allah so that they may disbelieve in the blessing of Allah and so that they may enjoy themselves by both of them. So in both verbs it is the lām of purpose. It was also said: both are imperative lāms for threat and warning: that is, "disbelieve in what We have given you of blessing, and enjoy yourselves." This reading supports this possibility; it is the reading of Ubayy, "wa-tamatta'ū." This possibility of both meanings applies only to the reading of Abu 'Amr, Ibn 'Amir, 'Asim and Warsh with kasra on the lām. As for the reading of the majority with sukun, there is no disagreement that it is the imperative lām. And in His saying ﴿fa-sawfa ya'lamūn﴾ ("but they will come to know") there is a great threat for them, that is: they will soon come to know the outcome of that and the calamity upon them in it.

﴿Have they not seen that We made a sanctuary secure while people are being snatched from around them?﴾ That is: have they not looked – meaning the disbelievers of Quraysh – that We made this their sanctuary a secure sanctuary, in which its resident is safe from raiding, killing, captivity and plunder; so they were in peace and well-being from what others among the Arabs were in, for they are at every moment struck by raids, their wealth is seized by invaders, their blood is shed by armies, and their sanctities and wealth are violated by the rogues and devils of the Arabs. The clause ﴿while people are being snatched from around them﴾ is in a place of accusative as a circumstantial state, that is: they are seizing those around them by killing, captivity and plunder. And "al-khatf" means taking with speed; its realization has already passed in Surah al-Qasas. ﴿Then in falsehood do they believe?﴾ That is: polytheism, after the proof of Allah has become manifest against them and they have acknowledged what necessitates monotheism. ﴿And in the blessing of Allah do they deny?﴾ They make their disbelief in place of their gratitude. In this interrogation there is a rebuke and reproach beyond measure.

﴿And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah or denies the truth when it has come to him?﴾ That is: there is no one more unjust than him, namely one who claims that Allah has a partner. ﴿Or denies the truth when it has come to him﴾: that is, he denies the Messenger to whom he was sent and the Book that He sent down to His Messenger.

Al-Suddi said: he denied the Oneness (tawhid). The apparent meaning includes whatever truly qualifies as being true.

Then He threatened and warned the deniers, saying: ﴿Is there not in Hell a dwelling for the disbelievers?﴾ That is: a place in which they will settle. The interrogative is for affirmation, and the meaning is: do they not deserve to abide therein, since they have done what they have done?

Then, when He had mentioned the condition of the polytheists who deny the Oneness and are ungrateful for the blessings of Allah, He followed it with the condition of His righteous servants, saying: ﴿And those who strive for Us, We will surely guide them to Our paths.﴾ That is: they strove in the matter of Allah seeking His good pleasure and hoping for what is with Him of good; "We will surely guide them to Our paths," that is, the way that leads to Us.

Ibn 'Atiyyah said: It is a Meccan verse, revealed before the obligation of conventional fighting (jihad al-'urfi); it is a general jihad in the religion of Allah and seeking His good pleasure. It was also said: this verse was revealed concerning worship.

Ibrahim ibn Adham said: It is about those who act according to what they know. ﴿And indeed, Allah is with the doers of good﴾ by victory and help, and whoever is with Him is not forsaken. The emphatic lām entered upon "ma'a" with the interpretation that it is a noun, or on the basis that it is a particle, and it was entered upon it to convey the meaning of permanence, as you say: "Indeed Zayd is in the house." The discussion is established in the science of grammar.

The commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 29, verses 56–69 (part 2 of 2):

It has been related by Ibn Mardawayh, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When this verse was revealed, ﴿Indeed, you will die, and indeed they will die﴾ [al-Zumar: 30], I said: 'O Lord, will all creation die while the prophets remain?' Then this was revealed: ﴿Every soul will taste death. Then to Us you will be returned﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 57]."

But consider the soundness of this report. After hearing the word of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿Indeed, you will die, and indeed they will die﴾, the Prophet (ﷺ) knows that he will die, and he knows that the prophets before him have died, and that he is the Seal of the Prophets. So how could there arise from this verse what Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) asked about, namely his statement, "Will creation die while the prophets remain?" It is therefore likely that this report is not authentic, whether traced to the Prophet (marfu', i.e., attributed to the Prophet) or stopping at a Companion (mawquf, i.e., attributed to a Companion).

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi and Ibn Asakir have related, and al-Suyuti said it is with a weak chain of narration (isnad), on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: "I went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) until he entered some of the gardens of Madinah, and he began to pick dates and eat. He said to me: 'Why do you not eat?' I said: 'I have no desire for it, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'But I have a desire for it, and this is the morning of the fourth day since I last tasted food and did not find any. If I wished, I could ask my Lord and He would give me the like of the kingdom of Kisra and Qaysar. So what will become of you, O son of Umar, when you remain among a people who hoard the provision of their year, and whose certainty grows weak?' He (Ibn Umar) said: 'By Allah, we did not leave, nor did we move, until there was revealed: ﴿And how many a creature does not carry its provision﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 60], and so on.' Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Indeed Allah has not commanded me to hoard the world, nor to follow desires. Verily, I do not hoard a dinar or a dirham, nor do I store provision for tomorrow.'"

This report contains severe disapproval (nakarah, i.e., a report that conflicts with established reports), because it contradicts what the Prophet (ﷺ) used to do, for he would give his wives their provision for the year, as is established in the reliable books of hadith.

In its chain is Abu al-'Atuf al-Jawzi, and he is weak.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim have related, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, concerning ﴿And indeed, the Hereafter is the [true] life﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 64], that he said: "It is everlasting."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman have related on the authority of Abu Ja'far, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "How strange, how very strange, is the one who believes in the abode of life, yet strives for the abode of delusion." This is a mursal report (a report in which the chain omits a Companion and goes directly from a Successor to the Prophet).

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 29, verses 56–69 (part 1 of 2):

When He, glory be to Him, mentioned the condition of the disbelievers among the People of the Book and the polytheists, grouped them together in the warning, and made them among the people of the Fire, their obstinacy intensified, their corruption increased, and they strove to harm the Muslims in every way. So Allah, glory be to Him, said: ﴿O My servants who have believed﴾. He attributed them to Himself after addressing them, as an honour and a mark of dignity. The phrase ﴿who have believed﴾ is a descriptive qualifier, either explanatory or distinguishing. ﴿Indeed, My earth is spacious﴾: if you are in straitened circumstances in Makkah due to displaying faith and due to the plotting of the disbelievers, then leave it, so that My worship alone may be made easy for you and made smooth for you.

Then He, glory be to Him, described those chambers, saying: ﴿Beneath them rivers flow﴾, that is: from beneath the chambers; ﴿abiding therein﴾, that is: in the chambers, they will never die forever, or in Paradise; the first is preferable. ﴿How excellent is the reward of the workers﴾: the object of praise is omitted, meaning: how excellent is the reward of the workers is their reward. The meaning is: those who work at righteous deeds.

Then He described these workers, saying: Those who were patient in the hardships of obligation and in the harm inflicted on them by the polytheists, and it is permissible for it to be accusative as a praise. ﴿And upon their Lord they rely﴾, that is: they entrust their affairs to Him in every undertaking and every withdrawal.

Had they known anything of knowledge, they would not have preferred over it the perishable, troubled abode.

Then, glory be to Him, made clear that the thing preventing them from faith is nothing but the mere influence of life. So He said: ﴿And when they board ships, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion.﴾ That is: when their hope of life is cut off and they fear drowning, they return to the natural disposition, so they call upon Allah alone, appearing as those sincere to Him in religion through the sincerity of their intentions, and abandoning at that time the calling upon idols, knowing that none other than Allah – glory be to Him – can remove this great hardship that has descended upon them. ﴿But when He delivers them to the land, at once they associate others with Him.﴾ That is: they suddenly returned to polytheism and called upon other than Allah, glory be to Him.

Riding (rukūb) means being elevated, and it is transitive by itself; it was made transitive by the word "fī" only to indicate that the thing ridden is in itself of the category of places.

The clause ﴿while people are being snatched from around them﴾ is in a place of accusative as a circumstantial state, that is: they are seizing those around them by killing, captivity and plunder. In this interrogation there is a rebuke and reproach beyond measure.

﴿And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah or denies the truth when it has come to him?﴾ That is: there is no one more unjust than him, namely one who claims that Allah has a partner. ﴿Or denies the truth when it has come to him﴾: that is, he denies the Messenger to whom he was sent and the Book that He sent down to His Messenger.

Al-Suddi said: he denied the Oneness (tawhid). The apparent meaning includes whatever truly qualifies as being true.

Then He threatened and warned the deniers, saying: ﴿Is there not in Hell a dwelling for the disbelievers?﴾ That is: a place in which they will settle. The interrogative is for affirmation, and the meaning is: do they not deserve to abide therein, since they have done what they have done?

Ibrahim ibn Adham said: It is about those who act according to what they know. ﴿And indeed, Allah is with the doers of good﴾ by victory and help, and whoever is with Him is not forsaken. The emphatic lām entered upon "ma'a" with the interpretation that it is a noun, or on the basis that it is a particle, and it was entered upon it to convey the meaning of permanence, as you say: "Indeed Zayd is in the house." The discussion is established in the science of grammar.

The commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 29, verses 56–69 (part 2 of 2):

It has been related by Ibn Mardawayh, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When this verse was revealed, ﴿Indeed, you will die, and indeed they will die﴾ [al-Zumar: 30], I said: 'O Lord, will all creation die while the prophets remain?' Then this was revealed: ﴿Every soul will taste death. Then to Us you will be returned﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 57]."

But consider the soundness of this report. After hearing the word of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿Indeed, you will die, and indeed they will die﴾, the Prophet (ﷺ) knows that he will die, and he knows that the prophets before him have died, and that he is the Seal of the Prophets. So how could there arise from this verse what Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) asked about, namely his statement, "Will creation die while the prophets remain?" It is therefore likely that this report is not authentic, whether traced to the Prophet (marfu', i.e., attributed to the Prophet) or stopping at a Companion (mawquf, i.e., attributed to a Companion).

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi and Ibn Asakir have related, and al-Suyuti said it is with a weak chain of narration (isnad), on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: "I went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) until he entered some of the gardens of Madinah, and he began to pick dates and eat. He said to me: 'Why do you not eat?' I said: 'I have no desire for it, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'But I have a desire for it, and this is the morning of the fourth day since I last tasted food and did not find any. If I wished, I could ask my Lord and He would give me the like of the kingdom of Kisra and Qaysar. So what will become of you, O son of Umar, when you remain among a people who hoard the provision of their year, and whose certainty grows weak?' He (Ibn Umar) said: 'By Allah, we did not leave, nor did we move, until there was revealed: ﴿And how many a creature does not carry its provision﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 60], and so on.' Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Indeed Allah has not commanded me to hoard the world, nor to follow desires. Verily, I do not hoard a dinar or a dirham, nor do I store provision for tomorrow.'"

This report contains severe disapproval (nakarah, i.e., a report that conflicts with established reports), because it contradicts what the Prophet (ﷺ) used to do, for he would give his wives their provision for the year, as is established in the reliable books of hadith.

In its chain is Abu al-'Atuf al-Jawzi, and he is weak.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim have related, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, concerning ﴿And indeed, the Hereafter is the [true] life﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 64], that he said: "It is everlasting."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman have related on the authority of Abu Ja'far, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "How strange, how very strange, is the one who believes in the abode of life, yet strives for the abode of delusion." This is a mursal report (a report in which the chain omits a Companion and goes directly from a Successor to the Prophet).

The phrase ﴿who have believed﴾ is a descriptive qualifier, either explanatory or distinguishing. ﴿Indeed, My earth is spacious﴾: if you are in straitened circumstances in Makkah due to displaying faith and due to the plotting of the disbelievers, then leave it, so that My worship alone may be made easy for you and made smooth for you.

103 Al-Zajjaj said: They were commanded to emigrate from the place where it is not possible for them to worship Allah. Likewise, whoever is in a land where sins are committed and cannot change that is obliged to emigrate to where he can prepare himself to worship Allah with the worship due to Him.

Mutarrif ibn al-Shikhkhir said: The meaning is: indeed My mercy is vast and My provision for you is ample, so seek it in the earth.

It was also said: The meaning is: indeed My earth, which is the earth of Paradise, is spacious, so worship Me and I will make you inherit it.

The accusative of ﴿iyya-ya﴾ (Me) is by a hidden verb, meaning: so worship Me.

Then He, glory be to Him, made them fear death in order to ease for them the matter of emigration, and said: ﴿Every soul shall taste death; then to Us you will be returned﴾. That is: every soul among souls will certainly experience the bitterness of death, so leaving homelands and parting from brothers and close friends should not be difficult for you. Then the return is to Allah by death and resurrection, not to anyone else. So every living being is on a journey to the abode of permanence, however long he remains in this abode.

The meaning of ﴿lanubawwi'annahum﴾ (We will surely settle them) is: We will surely cause them to descend into the chambers of Paradise, which are its upper parts. Ibn 'Amir read ﴿inna ardi﴾ with fatha on the ya', while the rest read it with sukun.

Al-Sulami and Abu Bakr on the authority of 'Asim read ﴿yarji'un﴾ with the ya' (third person), while the rest read it with the ta' (second person).

Then He, glory be to Him, described those chambers, saying: ﴿Beneath them rivers flow﴾, that is: from beneath the chambers; ﴿abiding therein﴾, that is: in the chambers, they will never die forever, or in Paradise; the first is preferable. ﴿How excellent is the reward of the workers﴾: the object of praise is omitted, meaning: how excellent is the reward of the workers is their reward. Then He described these workers, saying: Those who were patient in the hardships of obligation and in the harm inflicted on them by the polytheists, and it is permissible for it to be accusative as a praise. ﴿And upon their Lord they rely﴾, that is: they entrust their affairs to Him in every undertaking and every withdrawal.

It was also said: the meaning is: "and how many a creature."

So how would they not rely upon Allah, with their strength and their capacity over the means of livelihood, just as it relies upon Allah despite its weakness and incapacity?

Al-Hasan said: It eats in its time; it stores nothing.

Mujahid said: It means birds and beasts, which eat with their mouths and carry nothing. And He is the All-Hearing who hears every thing heard, the All-Knowing of every thing known.

Then, glory be to Him, He mentioned the condition of the polytheists of Makkah and others, and the listener marvels at their acknowledging that He is their Creator and Provider, yet they do not affirm His oneness and abandon the worship of others. So He said: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon?" they would surely say, "Allah."﴾ That is: He created them; they cannot deny that, nor are they able to reject it. ﴿So how are they turned away?﴾ That is: how are they diverted from acknowledging His singularity in divinity, and that He alone has no partner? The interrogative is for denial and remoteness.

For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed Allah is Knowing of all things﴾, He knows what is good for His servants and what is corrupt for them.

So He said: ﴿Say, "Praise is to Allah." But most of them do not reason.﴾ That is: I praise Allah for making the truth with you and for manifesting your proof against them. Then He condemned them, saying: "But most of them do not reason," meaning the things that sensible people reason about.

Then, glory be to Him, He pointed to the belittling of this world and that it is of the nature of play and amusement, and that the true abode is the abode of the Hereafter. Then, glory be to Him, made clear that the thing preventing them from faith is nothing but the mere influence of life. This reading supports this possibility; it is the reading of Ubayy, "wa-tamatta'ū." This possibility of both meanings applies only to the reading of Abu 'Amr, Ibn 'Amir, 'Asim and Warsh with kasra on the lām. As for the reading of the majority with sukun, there is no disagreement that it is the imperative lām. The meaning of ﴿does not carry its provision﴾ is: it is not able to carry its provision due to its weakness, and it does not store it. Rather, Allah provides for it from His bounty and provides for you. So how would they not rely upon Allah, with their strength and their capacity over the means of livelihood, just as it relies upon Allah despite its weakness and incapacity?

Al-Hasan said: It eats in its time; it stores nothing.

Mujahid said: It means birds and beasts, which eat with their mouths and carry nothing. And He is the All-Hearing who hears every thing heard, the All-Knowing of every thing known.

Then, glory be to Him, He mentioned the condition of the polytheists of Makkah and others, and the listener marvels at their acknowledging that He is their Creator and Provider, yet they do not affirm His oneness and abandon the worship of others. So He said: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon?" they would surely say, "Allah."﴾ That is: He created them; they cannot deny that, nor are they able to reject it. ﴿So how are they turned away?﴾ That is: how are they diverted from acknowledging His singularity in divinity, and that He alone has no partner? The interrogative is for denial and remoteness.

For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed Allah is Knowing of all things﴾, He knows what is good for His servants and what is corrupt for them.

﴿And if you asked them, "Who sent down water from the sky and gave life thereby to the earth after its death?" they would surely say, "Allah."﴾ That is: He sent it down and Allah gave life to the earth by it; they acknowledge that, finding no way to deny it.

Then, when they acknowledged this acknowledgment in these verses, which necessitates the falsity of what they are upon of polytheism and not singling out Allah, glory be to Him, in worship, He commanded His Messenger, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, to praise Allah for their acknowledgment and non-denial, despite their obstinacy and their rigidity in rejecting everything the Messenger of Allah brought of monotheism. So He said: ﴿Say, "Praise is to Allah." But most of them do not reason.﴾ That is: I praise Allah for making the truth with you and for manifesting your proof against them.
